hadithText: I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "The reward of deeds depends upon the intentions and every person will get the reward according to what he has intended. So whoever emigrated for worldly benefits or for a woman to marry, his emigration was for what he emigrated for."
theme: How the Divine Revelation started being revealed to Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him)

questions.question: What is the primary message of this hadith regarding deeds and rewards?
options: Physical actions matter more than intentions
Only major deeds are rewarded by Allah
Rewards are based on intentions behind actions
Rewards are equal for all good deeds
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that the reward of deeds depends upon the intentions, and every person gets reward according to what they intended

questions.question: If someone performs Hajj primarily to gain social status rather than pleasing Allah, they will still receive the full spiritual reward.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: According to this hadith, rewards are based on intentions. Performing religious acts for worldly gains rather than Allah's pleasure diminishes or eliminates the spiritual reward

questions.question: How can you apply the lesson of this hadith in your daily worship?
options: Regularly check my intentions before acts of worship
Seek to purify my heart from worldly motives in worship
All of the above
Focus on sincerity rather than just outward appearance of deeds
questions.explanation: All these actions help implement the hadith's teaching by ensuring our deeds are performed with pure intentions for Allah's pleasure alone

hadithText: Al-Harith bin Hisham asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! How is the Divine Inspiration revealed to you?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "Sometimes it is (revealed) like the ringing of a bell, this form of Inspiration is the hardest of all and then this state passes off after I have grasped what is inspired. Sometimes the Angel comes in the form of a man and talks to me and I grasp whatever he says." 'Aisha added: Verily I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) being inspired divinely on a very cold day and noticed the sweat dropping from his forehead (as the Inspiration was over).

questions.question: According to the hadith, what are the two main ways Divine Inspiration was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: Like ringing of a bell and angel in human form
Through natural signs and miracles
Through dreams and visions only
Through written scrolls and direct speech
questions.explanation: The Prophet clearly described two methods: sometimes like the ringing of a bell (most difficult form) and sometimes through an angel appearing as a man

questions.question: The physical effects described in this hadith show that receiving revelation was an intense spiritual experience for the Prophet (ﷺ)
options: False
True
questions.explanation: Aisha's testimony about sweat dropping from the Prophet's forehead on a cold day demonstrates the physical intensity of receiving revelation

questions.question: How can we apply the lessons from this hadith about the Prophet's experience with revelation in our daily lives?
options: Learn about Allah's wisdom in choosing revelation methods
All of the above
Appreciate the difficulty of revelation and value the Quran more
Understand the Prophet's sincerity and strengthen our faith
questions.explanation: This hadith helps us appreciate the Quran's divine origin, understand the Prophet's noble character, and strengthen our connection with Islamic teachings

hadithText: (the mother of the faithful believers) The commencement of the Divine Inspiration to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was in the form of good dreams which came true like bright daylight, and then the love of seclusion was bestowed upon him. He used to go in seclusion in the cave of Hira where he used to worship (Allah alone) continuously for many days before his desire to see his family. He used to take with him the journey food for the stay and then come back to (his wife) Khadija to take his food likewise again till suddenly the Truth descended upon him while he was in the cave of Hira. The angel came to him and asked him to read. The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "I do not know how to read." The Prophet (ﷺ) added, "The angel caught me (forcefully) and pressed me so hard that I could not bear it any more. He then released me and again asked me to read and I replied, 'I do not know how to read.' Thereupon he caught me again and pressed me a second time till I could not bear it any more. He then released me and again asked me to read but again I replied, 'I do not know how to read (or what shall I read)?' Thereupon he caught me for the third time and pressed me, and then released me and said, 'Read in the name of your Lord, who has created (all that exists), created man from a clot. Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous." (96.1, 96.2, 96.3) Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) returned with the Inspiration and with his heart beating severely. Then he went to Khadija bint Khuwailid and said, "Cover me! Cover me!" They covered him till his fear was over and after that he told her everything that had happened and said, "I fear that something may happen to me." Khadija replied, "Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep good relations with your kith and kin, help the poor and the destitute, serve your guests generously and assist the deserving calamity-afflicted ones." Khadija then accompanied him to her cousin Waraqa bin Naufal bin Asad bin 'Abdul 'Uzza, who, during the pre-Islamic Period became a Christian and used to write the writing with Hebrew letters. He would write from the Gospel in Hebrew as much as Allah wished him to write. He was an old man and had lost his eyesight. Khadija said to Waraqa, "Listen to the story of your nephew, O my cousin!" Waraqa asked, "O my nephew! What have you seen?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) described whatever he had seen. Waraqa said, "This is the same one who keeps the secrets (angel Gabriel) whom Allah had sent to Moses. I wish I were young and could live up to the time when your people would turn you out." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) asked, "Will they drive me out?" Waraqa replied in the affirmative and said, "Anyone (man) who came with something similar to what you have brought was treated with hostility; and if I should remain alive till the day when you will be turned out then I would support you strongly." But after a few days Waraqa died and the Divine Inspiration was also paused for a while.

questions.question: What was the initial form of Divine Inspiration that came to Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) according to this hadith?
options: Direct revelation from Angel Gabriel
Inner spiritual experiences
Good dreams that came true
Divine messages during prayer
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that the commencement of Divine Inspiration was in the form of good dreams which came true like bright daylight, before the first revelation in Cave Hira

questions.question: When faced with difficult situations, we should immediately seek support from trustworthy people who can provide wise counsel, just as the Prophet sought comfort and guidance from Khadija and Waraqa
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith shows the Prophet turning to his wife Khadija for comfort and then to the knowledgeable Waraqa for understanding, demonstrating the importance of seeking support and counsel during challenging times

questions.question: How can you apply the lessons from this hadith about facing challenges with trust in Allah?
options: All of the above
I will trust Allah's plan during difficult moments
I will support others facing challenges as Khadija supported the Prophet
I will seek knowledge and understanding when confused
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us to maintain trust in Allah during trials, seek knowledge and counsel when needed, and support others in their difficulties - all valuable applications for our spiritual growth

hadithText: "While I was walking, all of a sudden I heard a voice from the sky. I looked up and saw the same angel who had visited me at the cave of Hira' sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I got afraid of him and came back home and said, 'Wrap me (in blankets).' And then Allah revealed the following Holy Verses (of Quran): 'O you (i.e. Muhammad)! wrapped up in garments!' Arise and warn (the people against Allah's Punishment),... up to 'and desert the idols.' (74.1-5) After this the revelation started coming strongly, frequently and regularly."

questions.question: What is the primary message conveyed through this hadith about the Prophet's mission?
options: To arise and warn people against Allah's punishment
To retreat from society and focus on personal worship
To establish political leadership in Mecca
To compile the Quran into a single book
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically mentions the revelation commanding the Prophet to 'Arise and warn (the people against Allah's Punishment)' and to 'desert the idols,' establishing his core mission of calling people to monotheism.

questions.question: According to this hadith, when faced with challenging divine commands, one should completely withdraw from their responsibilities.
options: False
True
questions.explanation: Although the Prophet initially felt fear and sought comfort, Allah's command immediately directed him to arise and fulfill his duty, teaching us to overcome initial fears and fulfill our obligations.

questions.question: How can you apply the lessons from this hadith in your daily life?
options: Strengthen commitment to regular worship and Quran study
All of the above
Warn others gently against wrong actions when possible
Overcome personal fears to fulfill religious duties
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches multiple valuable lessons about courage in da'wah, gentle guidance, and consistent devotion - all essential for spiritual growth.

hadithText: Ibn 'Abbas in the explanation of the statement of Allah "Move not your tongue concerning (the Quran) to make haste therewith." (75.16) said "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to bear the revelation with great trouble and used to move his lips (quickly) with the Inspiration." Ibn 'Abbas moved his lips saying, "I am moving my lips in front of you as Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to move his." Said moved his lips saying: "I am moving my lips, as I saw Ibn 'Abbas moving his." Ibn 'Abbas added, "So Allah revealed 'Move not your tongue concerning (the Qur'an) to make haste therewith. It is for Us to collect it and to give you (O Muhammad) the ability to recite it (the Quran)' (75.16-17) which means that Allah will make him (the Prophet) remember the portion of the Qur'an which was revealed at that time by heart and recite it. The statement of Allah: 'And when we have recited it to you (O Muhammad through Gabriel) then you follow its (Quran) recital' (75.18) means 'listen to it and be silent.' Then it is for Us (Allah) to make it clear to you' (75.19) means 'Then it is (for Allah) to make you recite it (and its meaning will be clear by itself through your tongue). Afterwards, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to listen to Gabriel whenever he came and after his departure he used to recite it as Gabriel had recited it."

questions.question: What was the main reason Allah revealed 'Move not your tongue concerning (the Quran) to make haste therewith' to Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: Because the Prophet was reciting too loudly
To correct mistakes in his pronunciation
To teach him to be patient and let Allah help him memorize the revelation
Because he was interrupting Angel Gabriel
questions.explanation: The hadith explains that Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) used to move his lips quickly with the revelation, and Allah taught him to be patient and trust that Allah would make him remember and recite the Quran perfectly

questions.question: According to this hadith, after receiving revelation from Gabriel, Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) would immediately start teaching it to others without waiting for proper understanding
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith states that after Gabriel's departure, the Prophet would recite it exactly as Gabriel had recited it, indicating he waited for complete revelation and proper recitation before sharing

questions.question: How can we apply the lesson from this hadith in our own Quran recitation and learning?
options: Be patient and trust Allah's help in memorization
Avoid rushing through recitation
Listen attentively when learning Quran
All of the above
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us the importance of patience, trust in Allah, attentive listening, and avoiding haste in our Quranic studies - all essential qualities for proper learning and reflection

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was the most generous of all the people, and he used to reach the peak in generosity in the month of Ramadan when Gabriel met him. Gabriel used to meet him every night of Ramadan to teach him the Qur'an. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was the most generous person, even more generous than the strong uncontrollable wind (in readiness and haste to do charitable deeds).

questions.question: What is the main characteristic of Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) emphasized in this hadith?
options: His exceptional generosity, especially during Ramadan
His ability to memorize the Quran quickly
His knowledge of various languages
His physical strength and endurance
questions.explanation: The hadith repeatedly emphasizes the Prophet's generosity, describing him as 'the most generous of all people' and comparing his generosity to the 'strong uncontrollable wind'

questions.question: According to this hadith, Muslims should increase their charitable deeds during Ramadan following the Prophet's example
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically mentions the Prophet reached 'the peak in generosity in the month of Ramadan,' setting an example for Muslims to increase good deeds during this blessed month

questions.question: How can you follow the Prophet's example of generosity described in this hadith?
options: Increase charity and good deeds during Ramadan
All of the above
Be consistently generous throughout the year
Help others with urgency and eagerness
questions.explanation: The Prophet's example teaches us to be generous year-round, increase generosity in Ramadan, and perform charitable deeds with the haste and readiness of strong wind

hadithText: Abu Sufyan bin Harb informed me that Heraclius had sent a messenger to him while he had been accompanying a caravan from Quraish. They were merchants doing business in Sham (Syria, Palestine, Lebanon and Jordan), at the time when Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had truce with Abu Sufyan and Quraish infidels. So Abu Sufyan and his companions went to Heraclius at Ilya (Jerusalem). Heraclius called them in the court and he had all the senior Roman dignitaries around him. He called for his translator who, translating Heraclius's question said to them, "Who amongst you is closely related to that man who claims to be a Prophet?" Abu Sufyan replied, "I am the nearest relative to him (amongst the group)." Heraclius said, "Bring him (Abu Sufyan) close to me and make his companions stand behind him." Abu Sufyan added, Heraclius told his translator to tell my companions that he wanted to put some questions to me regarding that man (The Prophet) and that if I told a lie they (my companions) should contradict me." Abu Sufyan added, "By Allah! Had I not been afraid of my companions labeling me a liar, I would not have spoken the truth about the Prophet. The first question he asked me about him was: 'What is his family status amongst you?' I replied, 'He belongs to a good (noble) family amongst us.' Heraclius further asked, 'Has anybody amongst you ever claimed the same (i.e. to be a Prophet) before him?' I replied, 'No.' He said, 'Was anybody amongst his ancestors a king?' I replied, 'No.' Heraclius asked, 'Do the nobles or the poor follow him?' I replied, 'It is the poor who follow him.' He said, 'Are his followers increasing decreasing (day by day)?' I replied, 'They are increasing.' He then asked, 'Does anybody amongst those who embrace his religion become displeased and renounce the religion afterwards?' I replied, 'No.' Heraclius said, 'Have you ever accused him of telling lies before his claim (to be a Prophet)?' I replied, 'No. ' Heraclius said, 'Does he break his promises?' I replied, 'No. We are at truce with him but we do not know what he will do in it.' I could not find opportunity to say anything against him except that. Heraclius asked, 'Have you ever had a war with him?' I replied, 'Yes.' Then he said, 'What was the outcome of the battles?' I replied, 'Sometimes he was victorious and sometimes we.' Heraclius said, 'What does he order you to do?' I said, 'He tells us to worship Allah and Allah alone and not to worship anything along with Him, and to renounce all that our ancestors had said. He orders us to pray, to speak the truth, to be chaste and to keep good relations with our Kith and kin.' Heraclius asked the translator to convey to me the following, I asked you about his family and your reply was that he belonged to a very noble family. In fact all the Apostles come from noble families amongst their respective peoples. I questioned you whether anybody else amongst you claimed such a thing, your reply was in the negative. If the answer had been in the affirmative, I would have thought that this man was following the previous man's statement. Then I asked you whether anyone of his ancestors was a king. Your reply was in the negative, and if it had been in the affirmative, I would have thought that this man wanted to take back his ancestral kingdom. I further asked whether he was ever accused of telling lies before he said what he said, and your reply was in the negative. So I wondered how a person who does not tell a lie about others could ever tell a lie about Allah. I, then asked you whether the rich people followed him or the poor. You replied that it was the poor who followed him. And in fact all the Apostle have been followed by this very class of people. Then I asked you whether his followers were increasing or decreasing. You replied that they were increasing, and in fact this is the way of true faith, till it is complete in all respects. I further asked you whether there was anybody, who, after embracing his religion, became displeased and discarded his religion. Your reply was in the negative, and in fact this is (the sign of) true faith, when its delight enters the hearts and mixes with them completely. I asked you whether he had ever betrayed. You replied in the negative and likewise the Apostles never betray. Then I asked you what he ordered you to do. You replied that he ordered you to worship Allah and Allah alone and not to worship any thing along with Him and forbade you to worship idols and ordered you to pray, to speak the truth and to be chaste. If what you have said is true, he will very soon occupy this place underneath my feet and I knew it (from the scriptures) that he was going to appear but I did not know that he would be from you, and if I could reach him definitely, I would go immediately to meet him and if I were with him, I would certainly wash his feet.' Heraclius then asked for the letter addressed by Allah's Apostle which was delivered by Dihya to the Governor of Busra, who forwarded it to Heraclius to read. The contents of the letter were as follows: "In the name of Allah the Beneficent, the Merciful (This letter is) from Muhammad the slave of Allah and His Apostle to Heraclius the ruler of Byzantine. Peace be upon him, who follows the right path. Furthermore I invite you to Islam, and if you become a Muslim you will be safe, and Allah will double your reward, and if you reject this invitation of Islam you will be committing a sin by misguiding your Arisiyin (peasants). (And I recite to you Allah's Statement:) 'O people of the scripture! Come to a word common to you and us that we worship none but Allah and that we associate nothing in worship with Him, and that none of us shall take others as Lords beside Allah. Then, if they turn away, say: Bear witness that we are Muslims (those who have surrendered to Allah).' (3:64). Abu Sufyan then added, "When Heraclius had finished his speech and had read the letter, there was a great hue and cry in the Royal Court. So we were turned out of the court. I told my companions that the question of Ibn-Abi-Kabsha) (the Prophet (ﷺ) Muhammad) has become so prominent that even the King of Bani Al-Asfar (Byzantine) is afraid of him. Then I started to become sure that he (the Prophet) would be the conqueror in the near future till I embraced Islam (i.e. Allah guided me to it)." The sub narrator adds, "Ibn An-Natur was the Governor of llya' (Jerusalem) and Heraclius was the head of the Christians of Sham. Ibn An-Natur narrates that once while Heraclius was visiting ilya' (Jerusalem), he got up in the morning with a sad mood. Some of his priests asked him why he was in that mood? Heraclius was a foreteller and an astrologer. He replied, 'At night when I looked at the stars, I saw that the leader of those who practice circumcision had appeared (become the conqueror). Who are they who practice circumcision?' The people replied, 'Except the Jews nobody practices circumcision, so you should not be afraid of them (Jews). 'Just Issue orders to kill every Jew present in the country.' While they were discussing it, a messenger sent by the king of Ghassan to convey the news of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) to Heraclius was brought in. Having heard the news, he (Heraclius) ordered the people to go and see whether the messenger of Ghassan was circumcised. The people, after seeing him, told Heraclius that he was circumcised. Heraclius then asked him about the Arabs. The messenger replied, 'Arabs also practice circumcision.' (After hearing that) Heraclius remarked that sovereignty of the 'Arabs had appeared. Heraclius then wrote a letter to his friend in Rome who was as good as Heraclius in knowledge. Heraclius then left for Homs. (a town in Syrian and stayed there till he received the reply of his letter from his friend who agreed with him in his opinion about the emergence of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the fact that he was a Prophet. On that Heraclius invited all the heads of the Byzantines to assemble in his palace at Homs. When they assembled, he ordered that all the doors of his palace be closed. Then he came out and said, 'O Byzantines! If success is your desire and if you seek right guidance and want your empire to remain then give a pledge of allegiance to this Prophet (i.e. embrace Islam).' (On hearing the views of Heraclius) the people ran towards the gates of the palace like onagers but found the doors closed. Heraclius realized their hatred towards Islam and when he lost the hope of their embracing Islam, he ordered that they should be brought back in audience. (When they returned) he said, 'What already said was just to test the strength of your conviction and I have seen it.' The people prostrated before him and became pleased with him, and this was the end of Heraclius's story (in connection with his faith).

questions.question: What was the main conclusion Heraclius reached after questioning Abu Sufyan about Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: He decided to immediately attack the Muslims
He concluded Muhammad (ﷺ) was an imposter
He recognized the signs of prophethood in Muhammad (ﷺ)
He thought Muhammad (ﷺ) wanted to reclaim ancestral kingdom
questions.explanation: Heraclius systematically analyzed the characteristics of Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and found they matched the signs of true prophethood mentioned in previous scriptures

questions.question: According to this hadith, when learning about Islam, one should examine the character of the Prophet, the nature of his followers, and the consistency of his message - just as Heraclius did
options: False
True
questions.explanation: Heraclius demonstrated a methodical approach to verifying prophethood by examining multiple aspects including family background, truthfulness, teachings, and follower demographics

questions.question: How can you apply the lessons from Heraclius's investigation in your own spiritual journey?
options: Reflect on the consistency and truthfulness of Islamic message
Study the Prophet's character and teachings deeply
All of the above
Examine how Islam transforms people's lives
questions.explanation: Following Heraclius's example, we should comprehensively study Islam's evidences, the Prophet's exemplary character, and the transformative power of faith in our lives

hadithText:
Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Islam is based on (the following) five (principles):
1. To testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and Muhammad is Allah's Messenger (ﷺ).
2. To offer the (compulsory congregational) prayers dutifully and perfectly.
3. To pay Zakat (i.e. obligatory charity) . 
4. To perform Hajj. (i.e. Pilgrimage to Mecca)
5. To observe fast during the month of Ramadan.

questions.question: According to this hadith, what are the five fundamental pillars that Islam is based upon?
options: Testifying faith, five daily prayers, obligatory charity, pilgrimage, and Ramadan fasting
Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Hajj, and Sawm
Belief in Allah, Prayer, Charity, Pilgrimage, and Fasting
Faith, Prayer, Charity, Fasting, and Pilgrimage
questions.explanation: The hadith explicitly lists these five pillars in the exact order: testifying faith (Shahadah), prayer (Salah), charity (Zakat), pilgrimage (Hajj), and fasting (Sawm) during Ramadan

questions.question: A Muslim who performs Hajj but neglects daily prayers is fulfilling all the pillars mentioned in this hadith
options: False
True
questions.explanation: False. The hadith emphasizes performing all five pillars, not selectively choosing some while neglecting others. Daily prayers are equally obligatory as Hajj

questions.question: How can you strengthen your commitment to these five pillars in your daily life?
options: By learning their meanings and purposes
All of the above
By seeking knowledge to perform them correctly
By establishing consistent practice of each pillar
questions.explanation: A comprehensive approach involving knowledge, consistent practice, and proper understanding is essential for fulfilling these pillars with sincerity and excellence

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Faith (Belief) consists of more than sixty branches (i.e. parts). And Haya (This term "Haya" covers a large number of concepts which are to be taken together; amongst them are self respect, modesty, bashfulness, and scruple, etc.) is a part of faith."
theme: (What is said) regarding the deeds of faith

questions.question: According to the hadith, what is the relationship between Haya and faith?
options: Haya replaces other aspects of faith
Haya is one branch among more than sixty branches of faith
Haya is separate from faith
Haya is the most important aspect of faith
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that faith consists of more than sixty branches, and Haya is one part among them

questions.question: Practicing modesty and self-respect in daily interactions demonstrates living according to this hadith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Since Haya includes modesty, self-respect, and bashfulness, practicing these qualities in daily life reflects the teachings of this hadith

questions.question: How will you strengthen your faith by developing Haya according to this hadith?
options: I will maintain scruples in my dealings with others
All of the above
I will cultivate self-respect in my actions
I will practice modesty in speech and behavior
questions.explanation: Developing all aspects of Haya - modesty, self-respect, bashfulness, and scruples - collectively strengthens one's faith as taught in this hadith

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "A Muslim is the one who avoids harming Muslims with his tongue and hands. And a Muhajir (emigrant) is the one who gives up (abandons) all what Allah has forbidden."
theme: A Muslim is the one who avoids harming Muslims with his tongue and hands

questions.question: According to this hadith, what defines a true Muslim?
options: One who performs Hajj pilgrimage
One who fasts during Ramadan
One who avoids harming fellow Muslims with tongue and hands
One who prays five times daily
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that a Muslim is defined by avoiding harm to other Muslims through both speech and actions

questions.question: Spreading rumors about a fellow Muslim would violate the teachings of this hadith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Spreading rumors constitutes harm with the tongue, which the Prophet specifically warned against in this hadith

questions.question: How will you implement this hadith's teachings in your daily life?
options: I will monitor my speech to avoid hurting others
I will ensure my actions don't cause harm to fellow Muslims
I will strive to abandon all that Allah has forbidden
All of the above
questions.explanation: This hadith calls for comprehensive self-improvement - guarding our speech, actions, and avoiding all forbidden matters

hadithText: Some people asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), "Whose Islam is the best? i.e. (Who is a very good Muslim)?" He replied, "One who avoids harming the Muslims with his tongue and hands."
theme: Whose Islam is the best (Who is the best Muslim)?

questions.question: According to the hadith, what defines the best Muslim?
options: One who prays the most prayers
One who avoids harming Muslims with tongue and hands
One who gives the most charity
One who fasts the most
questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) clearly stated that the best Muslim is one who protects fellow Muslims from harm caused by their speech and actions

questions.question: Spreading rumors about a Muslim brother would violate the teaching of this hadith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Spreading rumors harms others with your tongue, which directly contradicts the Prophet's teaching about being the best Muslim

questions.question: How can you implement this hadith in your daily life?
options: Avoid physical harm and protect others' safety
Think before speaking about others
All of the above
Speak well of fellow Muslims and defend their honor
questions.explanation: Implementing this beautiful teaching requires being mindful of both our speech and actions toward all Muslims, protecting them from any harm we might cause

hadithText: A man asked the Prophet (ﷺ) , "What sort of deeds or (what qualities of) Islam are good?" The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, 'To feed (the poor) and greet those whom you know and those whom you do not Know (See Hadith No. 27).
theme: To feed (others) is a part of Islam

questions.question: According to this hadith, what are the two good deeds specifically mentioned by Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: Giving charity and visiting the sick
Praying regularly and fasting
Feeding the poor and greeting everyone
Reading Quran and attending mosque
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly mentioned feeding others and greeting both those we know and don't know as good Islamic deeds

questions.question: According to this hadith, we should only greet people we know personally
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically mentions greeting both those you know and those you do not know, promoting universal brotherhood

questions.question: How can you practically implement the teachings of this hadith in your daily life?
options: All of the above
Greet strangers with salam in public
Share food with neighbors in need
Donate to food banks regularly
questions.explanation: Implementing all these actions helps fulfill both aspects of the hadith - feeding others and spreading greetings

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "None of you will have faith till he wishes for his (Muslim) brother what he likes for himself."
theme: To like for one's (Muslim's) brother what one likes for himself is a part of faith

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is essential for complete faith?
options: Performing all daily prayers perfectly
Memorizing the entire Quran
Wishing for other Muslims what you wish for yourself
Giving charity regularly
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically states that faith is incomplete until one wishes for their Muslim brother what they wish for themselves

questions.question: If you enjoy financial security, you should also wish for your Muslim neighbor to have financial security
options: True
False
questions.explanation: This directly applies the hadith's teaching - wishing for others the same good you desire for yourself

questions.question: How can you practically implement this hadith in your daily life?
options: Help others achieve what I aspire to achieve
Celebrate others' successes as if they were my own
All of the above
Pray for others to receive the blessings I seek
questions.explanation: True implementation requires multiple approaches - rejoicing in others' happiness, actively helping them, and making sincere dua for them

hadithText: "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "By Him in Whose Hands my life is, none of you will have faith till he loves me more than his father and his children."
theme: To love the Messenger (Muhammad saws) is a part of faith

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is essential for complete faith?
options: Loving the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) more than one's father and children
Performing all five daily prayers
Giving charity regularly
Fasting during Ramadan
questions.explanation: The hadith explicitly states that faith is incomplete until one loves the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) more than even their closest family members

questions.question: If someone prioritizes their child's wishes over following the Prophet's teachings, they need to reflect on their level of faith according to this hadith
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that true faith requires loving the Prophet more than our own children, which means prioritizing his guidance over personal family preferences

questions.question: How can you practically demonstrate greater love for the Prophet (ﷺ) than for your family?
options: Follow his Sunnah in all actions
All of the above
Study his life and teachings daily
Defend his honor and share his message
questions.explanation: True love for the Prophet manifests through comprehensive commitment to learning, following, and propagating his noble example in our lives

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said "None of you will have faith till he loves me more than his father, his children and all mankind."

questions.question: What is the primary condition of complete faith (iman) according to this hadith?
options: Following all Islamic rituals perfectly
Loving Allah above all
Loving the Prophet more than anyone else
Being kind to parents and children
questions.explanation: The hadith explicitly states that complete faith requires loving the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) more than one's father, children, and all mankind

questions.question: According to this hadith, if someone prioritizes their child's wishes over following the Prophet's teachings, their faith is incomplete
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that complete faith requires loving the Prophet more than even our closest family members, which means prioritizing his teachings over personal attachments

questions.question: How can you practically demonstrate greater love for the Prophet in your daily life?
options: Study his life and teachings regularly
Follow his Sunnah in my actions
Defend his honor when needed
All of the above
questions.explanation: True love for the Prophet manifests through comprehensive commitment - learning about him, emulating his character, and protecting his legacy in all aspects of life

hadithText:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Whoever possesses the following three qualities will have the sweetness (delight) of faith: 1. The one to whom Allah and His Apostle becomes dearer than anything else. 
2. Who loves a person and he loves him only for Allah's sake. 
3. Who hates to revert to Atheism (disbelief) as he hates to be thrown into the fire."

questions.question: According to the hadith, what are the three qualities that give a person the sweetness of faith?
options: Being patient, grateful, and truthful
Having wealth, knowledge, and good health
Praying five times daily, fasting Ramadan, and giving charity
Loving Allah and His Messenger most, loving for Allah's sake, and hating disbelief
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically mentions these three qualities as the path to experiencing the delight of faith

questions.question: Loving someone primarily because they give you material benefits would fulfill the condition of 'loving for Allah's sake' mentioned in the hadith
options: False
True
questions.explanation: Loving for Allah's sake means loving someone purely for their faith and righteousness, not for worldly benefits

questions.question: How can you personally cultivate the three qualities mentioned in this hadith?
options: By focusing only on my personal spiritual growth
By avoiding all social relationships
By prioritizing Allah's pleasure in all decisions, building pure Islamic friendships, and strengthening my aversion to disbelief
By occasionally remembering these qualities
questions.explanation: Implementing all three aspects holistically is essential to truly experience the sweetness of faith as described by the Prophet

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Love for the Ansar is a sign of faith and hatred for the Ansar is a sign of hypocrisy."
theme: To love the Ansar is a sign of faith

questions.question: According to the hadith, what does loving the Ansar indicate about a person?
options: It is a sign of true faith
It makes one superior to others
It is optional but recommended
It guarantees entry to Paradise
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly stated that love for the Ansar is a sign of faith (iman), making it an indicator of genuine belief

questions.question: If someone consistently speaks negatively about the Ansar and their contributions to Islam, this hadith suggests they may have hypocrisy in their heart
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that hatred for the Ansar is a sign of hypocrisy (nifaq), so negative speech reflects this spiritual condition

questions.question: How can you practically demonstrate love for the Ansar in today's context?
options: All of the above
Speak respectfully about them and their legacy
Defend their honor when others criticize them
Study and appreciate their sacrifices for Islam
questions.explanation: All these actions demonstrate genuine love and appreciation for the Ansar, keeping their legacy alive in our hearts and communities

hadithText:
who took part in the battle of Badr and was a Naqib (a person heading a group of six persons), on the night of Al-'Aqaba pledge: Allah's Apostle said while a group of his companions were around him, "Swear allegiance to me for: 
1. Not to join anything in worship along with Allah. 
2. Not to steal. 
3. Not to commit illegal sexual intercourse. 
4. Not to kill your children. 
5. Not to accuse an innocent person (to spread such an accusation among people). 
6. Not to be disobedient (when ordered) to do good deed." 
The Prophet (ﷺ) added: "Whoever among you fulfills his pledge will be rewarded by Allah. And whoever indulges in any one of them (except the ascription of partners to Allah) and gets the punishment in this world, that punishment will be an expiation for that sin. And if one indulges in any of them, and Allah conceals his sin, it is up to Him to forgive or punish him (in the Hereafter)." 'Ubada bin As-Samit added: "So we swore allegiance for these." (points to Allah's Apostle)

questions.question: What is the primary message of this hadith regarding the pledge to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: It emphasizes the importance of wealth distribution in Islam
It focuses only on the political aspects of leadership
It describes the military strategy used during the Battle of Badr
It outlines key moral commitments that define a Muslim's character and faith
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly outlines six fundamental moral and spiritual commitments that form the basis of Islamic character, including avoiding shirk, major sins, and disobedience in good deeds

questions.question: According to this hadith, if someone commits one of these forbidden acts but Allah conceals their sin in this world, Allah may still hold them accountable in the Hereafter
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly stated that if Allah conceals someone's sin in this world, it remains up to Allah whether to forgive or punish them in the Hereafter

questions.question: How can you personally apply the teachings from this hadith in your daily life?
options: I will regularly examine my actions against these six commitments
I will be mindful not to falsely accuse others and protect innocent people's honor
All of the above
I will strive to avoid all forms of shirk and major sins mentioned
questions.explanation: Applying all these aspects demonstrates comprehensive commitment to the moral teachings in this hadith, helping strengthen both individual character and community wellbeing

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "A time will soon come when the best property of a Muslim will be sheep which he will take on the top of mountains and the places of rainfall (valleys) so as to flee with his religion from afflictions."
theme: To flee (run away) from Al-Fitn (afflictions and trials), is a part of religion

questions.question: What is the primary message of this hadith about facing trials and afflictions?
options: Muslims should become shepherds as their primary occupation
Material wealth is the best protection during times of trial
Fleeing to protect one's religion from fitnah is a religiously sanctioned action
Mountains and valleys are the safest places to live permanently
questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes that preserving one's faith during times of fitnah (trials/afflictions) is so important that fleeing to remote areas with basic possessions is justified

questions.question: According to this hadith, if a Muslim faces severe religious persecution that threatens their faith, they should prioritize staying in their community over protecting their religious commitment.
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that fleeing from fitnah to protect one's religion is part of faith, indicating that preserving religious commitment takes priority over remaining in a harmful environment

questions.question: How can you apply the wisdom of this hadith in your life when facing modern challenges to your faith?
options: I will identify and avoid environments that could corrupt my religious practice
I will be willing to make sacrifices to maintain my Islamic principles
All of the above
I will prioritize protecting my faith over worldly attachments when facing religious trials
questions.explanation: The comprehensive application involves recognizing the value of faith protection, avoiding corrupting influences, and being willing to make necessary sacrifices - all reflecting the hadith's core message

hadithText: Whenever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ordered the Muslims to do something, he used to order them deeds which were easy for them to do, (according to their strength and endurance). They said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! We are not like you. Allah has forgiven your past and future sins." So Allah's Apostle became angry and it was apparent on his face. He said, "I am the most Allah fearing, and know Allah better than all of you do."
theme: The statement of the Prophet (saws): "I know Allah Ta'ala better, than all of you do."

questions.question: What is the main message of this hadith regarding the Prophet's approach to teaching Islam?
options: The Prophet preferred to teach only advanced religious concepts
The Prophet expected everyone to achieve his same spiritual level
The Prophet always made religious practices accessible and manageable for people
The Prophet was easily angered by questions from his companions
questions.explanation: The hadith shows the Prophet's wisdom in making Islam easy to practice, as he 'used to order them deeds which were easy for them to do' according to their capabilities

questions.question: When teaching others about Islam, we should consider their individual capabilities and make the teachings manageable for them
options: True
False
questions.explanation: This follows the Prophet's example of making religious practices accessible and suitable for people's different capacities and circumstances

questions.question: How will you apply the lesson from this hadith in your own religious practice and teaching others?
options: I will avoid comparing my spiritual state with others and work within my capacity
All of the above
I will make Islam easy for myself and others by focusing on consistent small deeds
I will remember that Allah's mercy is vast and seek to know Him better through proper worship
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us multiple important lessons: making Islam practical, avoiding unnecessary comparisons, and striving for genuine God-consciousness in all our actions

hadithText:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Whoever possesses the following three qualities will taste the sweetness of faith: 
1. The one to whom Allah and His Apostle become dearer than anything else. 
2. Who loves a person and he loves him only for Allah's sake. 
3. Who hates to revert to disbelief (Atheism) after Allah has brought (saved) him out from it, as he hates to be thrown in fire."
theme: Whoever hates to revert to Kufr

questions.question: According to this hadith, what are the three qualities that enable a person to taste the sweetness of faith?
options: Having wealth, knowledge, and good character
Loving Allah and His Messenger most, loving for Allah's sake, and hating to return to disbelief
Helping others, speaking truth, and being patient
Praying five times daily, fasting Ramadan, and giving charity
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically mentions these three qualities as the path to experiencing the sweetness of faith

questions.question: Loving someone only because they are wealthy or influential fulfills the condition of 'loving for Allah's sake' mentioned in the hadith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Loving for Allah's sake means loving someone purely for their faith and righteousness, not for worldly benefits

questions.question: How can you practically implement the teachings of this hadith in your daily life?
options: Prioritize Allah and His Messenger above all else, build sincere relationships for Allah's sake, and strengthen my aversion to disbelief
Assume I'm already safe from disbelief without active effort
Focus only on my personal worship and ignore relationships with others
Occasionally remember Allah when convenient and maintain mixed intentions in relationships
questions.explanation: Implementing all three qualities mentioned in the hadith holistically is essential for tasting the sweetness of faith

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "When the people of Paradise will enter Paradise and the people of Hell will go to Hell, Allah will order those who have had faith equal to the weight of a grain of mustard seed to be taken out from Hell. So they will be taken out but (by then) they will be blackened (charred). Then they will be put in the river of Haya' (rain) or Hayat (life) (the Narrator is in doubt as to which is the right term), and they will revive like a grain that grows near the bank of a flood channel. Don't you see that it comes out yellow and twisted"
theme: The grades in superiority of the believers will be according to their good deeds

questions.question: What is the main message of this hadith regarding faith and salvation?
options: Good deeds alone determine who enters Paradise
Even the smallest amount of sincere faith can ultimately lead to salvation
People in Hell can never be rescued regardless of their faith
Only those with perfect faith will enter Paradise
questions.explanation: The hadith shows that even faith as small as a mustard seed, though initially punished, will eventually lead to salvation through Allah's mercy

questions.question: According to this hadith, a Muslim should never despair of Allah's mercy even if they have committed major sins, as long as they maintain some faith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith demonstrates that Allah's mercy can rescue believers from Hell based on even minimal faith, teaching us never to despair of divine compassion

questions.question: How can this hadith inspire you to strengthen your spiritual life?
options: All of the above
I will cherish and protect even the smallest acts of faith
I will never despair of Allah's mercy when I make mistakes
I will strive to increase my good deeds while relying on divine compassion
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us to value our faith, maintain hope in Allah's mercy, and continuously improve our deeds - all essential for spiritual growth

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "While I was sleeping I saw (in a dream) some people wearing shirts of which some were reaching up to the breasts only while others were even shorter than that. Umar bin Al-Khattab was shown wearing a shirt that he was dragging." The people asked, "How did you interpret it? (What is its interpretation) O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" He (the Prophet (ﷺ) ) replied, "It is the Religion."

questions.question: According to the Prophet's interpretation, what do the shirts in his dream represent?
options: Social status in the community
Physical clothing and modesty
Dreams about future events
The completeness of one's practice of Islam
questions.explanation: The Prophet explicitly stated that the shirts represent 'the Religion' - meaning how completely or incompletely people practice Islam

questions.question: Umar's long shirt dragging on the ground indicates he will have the most complete understanding and practice of Islam among the companions
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The longer shirt symbolizes deeper commitment and more comprehensive practice of the religion, as confirmed by the Prophet's interpretation

questions.question: How can you apply the lesson from this hadith in your daily life?
options: Evaluate which aspects of my faith need improvement
All of the above
Seek to implement Islamic teachings more completely in all areas of life
Strive to learn more about Islam to strengthen my practice
questions.explanation: This hadith encourages us to constantly assess and improve our practice of Islam, aiming for the comprehensive commitment symbolized by Umar's long shirt

hadithText: Once Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) passed by an Ansari (man) who was admonishing his brother regarding Haya'. On that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Leave him as Haya' is a part of faith." (See Hadith 9)
theme: Al-Haya (self-respect, modesty bashfulness, honour etc.) is a part of faith

questions.question: What is the main message of the hadith about the Ansari man being admonished for his Haya'?
options: Only Ansari people understand Haya' properly
People should not correct others about modesty
Haya' is optional for Muslims
Haya' (modesty) is an essential part of faith
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly stated 'Haya' is a part of faith,' emphasizing that modesty and self-respect are integral components of Islamic faith

questions.question: According to this hadith, if you see someone being excessively modest in a good way, you should encourage them to be less shy
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) told the man to leave his brother alone because Haya' is part of faith, indicating we should not discourage appropriate modesty

questions.question: How can you practically implement the lesson from this hadith in your daily life?
options: Appreciate and not criticize others' appropriate modesty
Recognize Haya' as strengthening my faith
All of the above
Cultivate modesty in speech, dress, and behavior
questions.explanation: Implementing this hadith requires a comprehensive approach - developing personal modesty, respecting others' modesty, and understanding its spiritual value

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "I have been ordered (by Allah) to fight against the people until they testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and that Muhammad is Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), and offer the prayers perfectly and give the obligatory charity, so if they perform that, then they save their lives and property from me except for Islamic laws and then their reckoning (accounts) will be done by Allah."
theme: (The Statement of Allah Jalla Jalalahu) "But if they repent [by rejecting Shirk (polytheism) and accept Islamic Monotheism] and perform As-Salat (Iqamat-as-Salat) and give Zakat then leave their way free."

questions.question: According to this hadith, what are the three fundamental conditions that protect one's life and property from fighting?
options: Testify La ilaha illallah and Muhammadur Rasulullah, establish prayer, and give Zakat
Read Quran daily, be honest, and help others
Believe in Allah, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj
Follow Islamic laws, pay taxes, and obey the ruler
questions.explanation: The hadith explicitly mentions testifying to Allah's oneness and Muhammad's prophethood, establishing prayer perfectly, and giving obligatory charity as the conditions for protection

questions.question: If someone accepts Islam and performs the obligatory prayers but neglects Zakat payments, they have fully met the conditions mentioned in this hadith
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that all three conditions - testimony of faith, prayer, and Zakat - must be fulfilled together to gain protection

questions.question: How can you personally ensure you're fulfilling the conditions mentioned in this hadith?
options: Focus only on prayer since it's most important
Just have faith in heart without outward actions
Regularly renew my testimony of faith, be diligent in prayers, and calculate/pay Zakat properly
Pay Zakat annually but be flexible about prayer times
questions.explanation: The comprehensive approach of maintaining all three pillars - faith declaration, prayer, and Zakat - reflects the complete message of the hadith and ensures we meet Allah's conditions fully

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was asked, "What is the best deed?" He replied, "To believe in Allah and His Apostle (Muhammad). The questioner then asked, "What is the next (in goodness)? He replied, "To participate in Jihad (religious fighting) in Allah's Cause." The questioner again asked, "What is the next (in goodness)?" He replied, "To perform Hajj (Pilgrim age to Mecca) 'Mubrur, (which is accepted by Allah and is performed with the intention of seeking Allah's pleasure only and not to show off and without committing a sin and in accordance with the traditions of the Prophet)."
theme: Whoever says that faith is action (good deeds)

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the highest ranking good deed?
options: Performing Jihad in Allah's cause
All good deeds are equal
Performing accepted Hajj
Belief in Allah and His Messenger
questions.explanation: The Prophet clearly ranked belief in Allah and His Messenger as the best deed, followed by Jihad, then Hajj Mubrur

questions.question: Performing Hajj for showing off to others would still be considered a highly ranked good deed according to this hadith
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith specifies Hajj must be 'Mubrur' - performed purely for Allah's pleasure without showing off or sin

questions.question: Based on this hadith's teachings, how can you strengthen your faith through actions?
options: Be ready to sacrifice for Allah's cause when needed
All of the above
Plan to perform Hajj with pure intentions when able
Strengthen my belief in Allah and His Messenger
questions.explanation: This hadith shows faith is strengthened by combining correct belief with righteous actions in their proper priority

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) distributed (Zakat) amongst (a group of) people while I was sitting there but Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) left a man whom I thought the best of the lot. I asked, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Why have you left that person? By Allah I regard him as a faithful believer." The Prophet (ﷺ) commented: "Or merely a Muslim." I remained quiet for a while, but could not help repeating my question because of what I knew about him. And then asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), "Why have you left so and so? By Allah! He is a faithful believer." The Prophet (ﷺ) again said, "Or merely a Muslim." And I could not help repeating my question because of what I knew about him. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "O Sa'd! I give to a person while another is dearer to me, for fear that he might be thrown on his face in the Fire by Allah."
theme: If one does not embrace Islam truly but does so by compulsion or for fear of being killed (then that man is not a believer)

questions.question: According to the hadith, why did Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) give Zakat to some people while leaving out a man Sa'd considered righteous?
options: To protect those whose faith might be weak from falling into Hellfire
Sa'd had misunderstood the man's financial situation
The Prophet (ﷺ) had personal dislike for that man
Because the man was already wealthy and didn't need Zakat
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) explained he gave to some while others were dearer to him, fearing Allah might throw the recipient on his face in the Fire if their faith wasn't sincere

questions.question: Based on this hadith, we should judge people's inner faith solely by their outward appearance and actions
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that only Allah knows what is in hearts - we cannot judge true faith by outward appearances alone

questions.question: How can this hadith influence your approach to charity and judging others?
options: I will focus on purifying my own intentions in worship and actions
I will remember that only Allah knows people's true faith and intentions
I will give charity sincerely without judging who 'deserves' it most
All of the above
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us multiple important lessons about charity, judging others, and purifying our own faith - all are valuable applications

hadithText: A person asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) . "What (sort of) deeds in or (what qualities of) Islam are good?" He replied, "To feed (the poor) and greet those whom you know and those whom you don't know."
theme: To greet is a part of Islam

questions.question: According to this hadith, what are the two good deeds specifically mentioned by Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: Feeding the poor and greeting people
Praying and fasting
Helping relatives and being honest
Reading Quran and giving charity
questions.explanation: The Prophet clearly identified feeding the poor and greeting both acquaintances and strangers as exemplary Islamic deeds

questions.question: According to this hadith, Muslims should only greet people they know personally
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The Prophet specifically mentioned greeting both those you know and those you don't know, emphasizing universal brotherhood

questions.question: How can you practically implement the teachings of this hadith in your daily life?
options: I will greet only Muslim friends
I will ignore strangers to avoid trouble
I will focus only on my prayers
I will donate to food charities and greet neighbors warmly
questions.explanation: Choosing to actively feed the needy and extend warm greetings to all reflects the comprehensive spirit of this hadith

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I was shown the Hell-fire and that the majority of its dwellers were women who were ungrateful." It was asked, "Do they disbelieve in Allah?" (or are they ungrateful to Allah?) He replied, "They are ungrateful to their husbands and are ungrateful for the favors and the good (charitable deeds) done to them. If you have always been good (benevolent) to one of them and then she sees something in you (not of her liking), she will say, 'I have never received any good from you."
theme: To be ungrateful to one's husband. And disbelief is of (different grades) lesser (or greater) degrees.

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the primary form of ingratitude that leads many women to Hell-fire?
options: Disbelieving in Allah completely
Being unkind to neighbors and relatives
Refusing to pray and fast
Being ungrateful to their husbands and denying their favors
questions.explanation: The Prophet specifically mentioned ingratitude towards husbands and denying their good deeds as the main issue, not outright disbelief in Allah

questions.question: If a husband has been consistently good to his wife, but she focuses on one minor fault and claims she never received any good from him, this constitutes the ingratitude mentioned in the hadith.
options: False
True
questions.explanation: This exact scenario is described in the hadith as an example of the ingratitude that leads to punishment

questions.question: How can you practically avoid the ingratitude warned about in this hadith?
options: All of the above
Always acknowledge and appreciate favors done for me
Regularly express gratitude to those who are good to me
Focus on the good qualities in others rather than minor faults
questions.explanation: Implementing all these practices helps cultivate a grateful heart and protects from the spiritual danger of ingratitude

hadithText: At Ar-Rabadha I met Abu Dhar who was wearing a cloak, and his slave, too, was wearing a similar one. I asked about the reason for it. He replied, "I abused a person by calling his mother with bad names." The Prophet said to me, 'O Abu Dhar! Did you abuse him by calling his mother with bad names You still have some characteristics of ignorance. Your slaves are your brothers and Allah has put them under your command. So whoever has a brother under his command should feed him of what he eats and dress him of what he wears. Do not ask them (slaves) to do things beyond their capacity (power) and if you do so, then help them.' "
theme: Sins are from ignorance and a sinner is not a disbeliever unless he worships others along with Allah 'Azza wa Jall

questions.question: What is the main lesson about how to treat those under our authority according to this hadith?
options: Only assign them easy tasks
Give them occasional time off work
Pay them well for their services
Treat them as brothers with equal food and clothing
questions.explanation: The Prophet explicitly teaches that slaves/servants are our brothers and we should feed them what we eat and dress them what we wear

questions.question: According to this hadith, if you assign someone a difficult task, you should help them complete it
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The Prophet specifically instructed: 'Do not ask them to do things beyond their capacity and if you do so, then help them'

questions.question: How will you apply the teachings from this hadith in your daily interactions?
options: All of the above
I will avoid insulting language and name-calling
I will treat household help with equal dignity
I will help others with tasks I assign them
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches comprehensive lessons about avoiding ignorance, treating others as brothers, and providing practical support - all essential for righteous conduct

hadithText: While I was going to help this man ('Ali Ibn Abi Talib), Abu Bakra met me and asked, "Where are you going?" I replied, "I am going to help that person." He said, "Go back for I have heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, 'When two Muslims fight (meet) each other with their swords, both the murderer as well as the murdered will go to the Hell-fire.' I said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! It is all right for the murderer but what about the murdered one?' Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "He surely had the intention to kill his companion."
theme: "And if two parties (or groups) from among the believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them both…" Allah has called them "believers"

questions.question: According to this hadith, why would both the murderer and murdered go to Hell-fire when two Muslims fight each other?
options: Both intended to kill each other
The murdered person was sinful
Fighting between Muslims is always forbidden
They broke their prayer commitments
questions.explanation: The Prophet clarified that even the murdered person goes to Hell because he also had the intention to kill his companion

questions.question: If you see two Muslim friends about to physically fight, you should try to help the one you think is more righteous
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches us to avoid taking sides and instead work to make peace between them, as helping either party in fighting could lead to sinful intentions

questions.question: How will you apply the lesson from this hadith in your daily life?
options: I will avoid taking sides in conflicts between Muslims
I will guard my intentions even in difficult situations
I will strive to be a peacemaker when disputes arise
All of the above
questions.explanation: This comprehensive approach helps prevent the sinful intentions and actions warned about in the hadith, promoting unity and peace

hadithText: When the following Verse was revealed: "It is those who believe and confuse not their belief with wrong (worshipping others besides Allah.)" (6:83), the companions of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) asked, "Who is amongst us who had not done injustice (wrong)?" Allah revealed: "No doubt, joining others in worship with Allah is a great injustice (wrong) indeed." (31.13)
theme: Dhulm (wrong) of one kind can be greater or lesser than that of another

questions.question: What is the main distinction about 'wrong' (dhulm) revealed in this hadith?
options: Wrong only applies to major sins
All wrongs are equal in severity
Shirk (associating partners with Allah) is the greatest form of wrong
Only physical harm counts as wrong
questions.explanation: The hadith clarifies that while the companions initially thought all wrongs were equal, Allah revealed that shirk is the greatest injustice, showing different wrongs have different severities

questions.question: According to this hadith, a Muslim who avoids shirk but commits minor sins is completely free from injustice (dhulm)
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith shows that while shirk is the greatest wrong, other injustices still exist - it distinguishes degrees of wrong rather than eliminating all other wrongs

questions.question: How will you apply the lesson from this hadith in your spiritual life?
options: All of the above
Prioritize avoiding shirk above all other sins
Be mindful that all sins are forms of injustice
Regularly renew my tawheed (Islamic monotheism)
questions.explanation: This comprehensive approach helps maintain pure faith while being conscious of all forms of injustice, applying the hadith's full lesson

hadithText:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The signs of a hypocrite are three: 
1. Whenever he speaks, he tells a lie. 
2. Whenever he promises, he always breaks it (his promise ). 
3. If you trust him, he proves to be dishonest. (If you keep something as a trust with him, he will not return it.)"

questions.question: According to the hadith, what are the three signs of a hypocrite?
options: Lying when speaking, breaking promises, and dishonesty in trusts
Praying irregularly, fasting occasionally, and giving charity rarely
Avoiding gatherings, neglecting greetings, and criticizing others
Speaking harshly, being impatient, and showing arrogance
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) clearly identified these three specific traits as signs of hypocrisy in one's character

questions.question: If someone consistently breaks their promises to you, this could be a sign of hypocrisy according to Islamic teachings
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Breaking promises is explicitly mentioned as one of the three signs of a hypocrite in this authentic hadith

questions.question: How can you protect yourself from developing hypocritical traits mentioned in this hadith?
options: Focus only on prayer and ignore other character aspects
Avoid making promises altogether to prevent breaking them
Always speak truthfully, fulfill all promises, and be honest in trusts
Only be honest with Muslims and not others
questions.explanation: The comprehensive approach of practicing truthfulness in speech, commitment to promises, and integrity in trusts aligns perfectly with the hadith's guidance

hadithText:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Whoever has the following four (characteristics) will be a pure hypocrite and whoever has one of the following four characteristics will have one characteristic of hypocrisy unless and until he gives it up.
1. Whenever he is entrusted, he betrays. 
2. Whenever he speaks, he tells a lie. 
3. Whenever he makes a covenant, he proves treacherous. 
4. Whenever he quarrels, he behaves in a very imprudent, evil and insulting manner."

questions.question: According to this hadith, what defines a complete hypocrite?
options: Someone who keeps promises but sometimes betrays
Someone who avoids quarrels
Someone who possesses all four mentioned characteristics
Someone who occasionally tells lies
questions.explanation: The Prophet clearly stated that possessing all four characteristics makes someone a pure hypocrite, while having even one requires repentance

questions.question: If someone regularly speaks lies but is honest in other matters, they still need to reform that specific characteristic to avoid hypocrisy
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that even one characteristic of hypocrisy remains until it is abandoned, requiring conscious effort to change

questions.question: How can you personally guard against hypocrisy based on this hadith?
options: All of the above
Always speak truthfully regardless of situation
Honor all trusts and covenants faithfully
Avoid insulting language during disagreements
questions.explanation: Comprehensive commitment to truthfulness, trustworthiness, and respectful conduct protects against all forms of hypocrisy mentioned in the hadith

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever establishes the prayers on the night of Qadr out of sincere faith and hoping to attain Allah's rewards (not to show off) then all his past sins will be forgiven."
theme: To establish the (Nawafil - voluntary) prayers on the night of Qadr is a part of faith

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the primary reward for praying on Laylat al-Qadr with sincere faith?
options: Becoming a scholar of Islam
Wealth and prosperity in this life
Guaranteed entry into Paradise without accountability
All past sins are forgiven
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that praying on Laylat al-Qadr with sincere faith and hope for Allah's reward results in forgiveness of all past sins

questions.question: If someone prays on Laylat al-Qadr primarily to show others how religious they are, they will still receive the full reward mentioned in the hadith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes that the prayer must be done with sincere faith and hoping for Allah's rewards, not for showing off (riya)

questions.question: How can you ensure you benefit from Laylat al-Qadr according to this hadith's teachings?
options: Increase voluntary prayers during the last ten nights of Ramadan
Pray with pure intention seeking only Allah's pleasure
All of the above
Make sincere dua for forgiveness and guidance
questions.explanation: Combining sincere worship, increased devotion during the blessed nights, and heartfelt supplication embodies the spirit of seeking Laylat al-Qadr as taught by the Prophet

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The person who participates in (Holy battles) in Allah's cause and nothing compels him to do so except belief in Allah and His Apostles, will be recompensed by Allah either with a reward, or booty (if he survives) or will be admitted to Paradise (if he is killed in the battle as a martyr). Had I not found it difficult for my followers, then I would not remain behind any sariya going for Jihad and I would have loved to be martyred in Allah's cause and then made alive, and then martyred and then made alive, and then again martyred in His cause."
theme: Al-Jihad (fighting tn Allah's Cause) is a part of faith

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the ONLY acceptable intention for participating in Jihad?
options: Social pressure from community
Belief in Allah and His Apostles
Political or nationalistic motives
Desire for worldly booty
questions.explanation: The Prophet specifically states that nothing should compel participation except belief in Allah and His Apostles, making pure faith the only valid intention

questions.question: Based on this hadith, a Muslim should actively seek opportunities for martyrdom in Allah's cause if they have the capability and means
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The Prophet's repeated desire to be martyred, revived, and martyred again demonstrates the high value of seeking martyrdom for Allah's cause when possible

questions.question: How can you embody the spirit of this hadith in your daily life?
options: Strive in Allah's cause through various forms of struggle
Develop love for sacrifice in Allah's path
All of the above
Purify my intentions in all deeds for Allah alone
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches us about pure intention, willingness to sacrifice, and comprehensive struggle - all essential aspects we should incorporate into our spiritual journey

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Whoever establishes prayers during the nights of Ramadan faithfully out of sincere faith and hoping to attain Allah's rewards (not for showing off), all his past sins will be forgiven."
theme: It is a part of faith to establish the (Nawafil — voluntary) prayers during the nights of Ramadan

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the promised reward for praying during Ramadan nights with sincere faith?
options: All past sins will be forgiven
Guaranteed entry into Paradise without accountability
Wealth and prosperity in this life
Special recognition among the Muslim community
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically states that all past sins will be forgiven for those who establish prayers during Ramadan nights with sincere faith and hoping for Allah's rewards

questions.question: Performing Taraweeh prayers to show off to others would still earn the full reward mentioned in this hadith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes that the prayers must be done 'faithfully out of sincere faith and hoping to attain Allah's rewards (not for showing off)' - showing off invalidates the sincerity required

questions.question: How can you ensure your night prayers during Ramadan align with the conditions mentioned in this hadith?
options: Focus on spiritual connection rather than social aspects
All of the above
Pray with pure intention only for Allah's pleasure
Consistently attend Taraweeh and Qiyam prayers
questions.explanation: All these actions help maintain the sincerity, consistency, and proper intention required to benefit from this blessed opportunity during Ramadan nights

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever observes fasts during the month of Ramadan out of sincere faith, and hoping to attain Allah's rewards, then all his past sins will be forgiven."
theme: To observe fasting (according to Islamic teachings)] during the month of Ramadan (sincerely and faithfully) hoping for Allah's Reward only, is a part of faith

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the primary condition for having past sins forgiven through Ramadan fasting?
options: Completing all 30 days of fasting without missing any
Fasting with sincere faith and hoping only for Allah's reward
Fasting while giving charity regularly
Fasting along with additional night prayers
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically emphasizes fasting with sincere faith (iman) and hoping for Allah's rewards as the key conditions for forgiveness of past sins

questions.question: If someone fasts Ramadan primarily to show others they are religious or to gain social approval, they will still receive the full reward mentioned in this hadith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith requires sincere faith and hoping for Allah's rewards only - fasting for show or social approval invalidates the sincerity required

questions.question: How can you ensure your Ramadan fasting aligns with the conditions mentioned in this hadith?
options: Avoid showing off or mentioning my fasting unnecessarily
Consciously seek Allah's reward and forgiveness throughout
All of the above
Regularly renew my intention for Allah's pleasure only
questions.explanation: All these actions help maintain the sincerity and God-consciousness required to fulfill the conditions mentioned in the hadith

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Religion is very easy and whoever overburdens himself in his religion will not be able to continue in that way. So you should not be extremists, but try to be near to perfection and receive the good tidings that you will be rewarded; and gain strength by worshipping in the mornings, the afternoons, and during the last hours of the nights." (See Fath-ul-Bari, Page 102, Vol 1).

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the main message about practicing religion?
options: Perfection means never making any mistakes in worship
Only morning and evening prayers are important
One must perform all possible worships to be a good Muslim
Religion should be practiced with ease and balance, avoiding extremism
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) clearly states that religion is easy and warns against overburdening oneself, emphasizing balance rather than extremism

questions.question: The hadith encourages taking breaks from worship to avoid exhaustion
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith doesn't suggest taking breaks but rather advises consistent, balanced worship at optimal times (mornings, afternoons, and last hours of nights) without overburdening oneself

questions.question: Based on this hadith, how can you apply its teachings in your daily life?
options: I will maintain consistent prayers without making religion difficult
I will seek balanced worship and avoid extreme practices
I will focus on morning, afternoon and night prayers with ease
All of the above
questions.explanation: All these applications reflect the hadith's core message of balanced, consistent worship without extremism

hadithText: When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina, he stayed first with his grandfathers or maternal uncles from Ansar. He offered his prayers facing Baitul-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for sixteen or seventeen months, but he wished that he could pray facing the Ka'ba (at Mecca). The first prayer which he offered facing the Ka'ba was the 'Asr prayer in the company of some people. Then one of those who had offered that prayer with him came out and passed by some people in a mosque who were bowing during their prayers (facing Jerusalem).
