He said addressing them, "By Allah, I testify that I have prayed with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) facing Mecca (Ka'ba).' Hearing that, those people changed their direction towards the Ka'ba immediately. Jews and the people of the scriptures used to be pleased to see the Prophet (ﷺ) facing Jerusalem in prayers but when he changed his direction towards the Ka'ba, during the prayers, they disapproved of it. Al-Bara' added, "Before we changed our direction towards the Ka'ba (Mecca) in prayers, some Muslims had died or had been killed and we did not know what to say about them (regarding their prayers.) Allah then revealed: And Allah would never make your faith (prayers) to be lost (i.e. the prayers of those Muslims were valid).' " (2:143).
theme: The (offering of) Salat (prayers) is a part of faith

questions.question: What was the main reason Allah revealed that the prayers of Muslims who died before the Qibla change were still valid?
options: To criticize the early Muslims for praying in the wrong direction
To show Allah's mercy and that sincere worship is never lost
To indicate that prayer direction doesn't matter in Islam
To suggest that only later prayers would be accepted
questions.explanation: Allah's revelation in Quran 2:143 demonstrates His infinite mercy, assuring believers that their sincere worship and faith are never wasted, even when external circumstances change

questions.question: When the Companions learned about the Qibla change to Ka'ba, they immediately adjusted their prayer direction without hesitation
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that when informed about the Prophet praying toward Ka'ba, the people in the mosque 'changed their direction towards the Ka'ba immediately,' demonstrating instant obedience to Allah's command

questions.question: How can we apply the lesson of this hadith in our daily practice of Islam?
options: Trust in Allah's mercy for past sincere worship even if I lacked perfect knowledge
All of the above
Follow religious guidance promptly when I learn it's authentic
Focus on the essence of worship while obeying prescribed forms
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us about immediate obedience, trust in Allah's compassion, and balancing spiritual essence with proper form - all essential for complete Islamic practice

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "If a person embraces Islam sincerely, then Allah shall forgive all his past sins, and after that starts the settlement of accounts, the reward of his good deeds will be ten times to seven hundred times for each good deed and one evil deed will be recorded as it is unless Allah forgives it."
theme: (What is said regarding the superiority of) a person who embraces Islam sincerely.

questions.question: According to this hadith, what happens to a person's past sins when they embrace Islam sincerely?
options: All past sins are forgiven by Allah
Past sins remain but are reduced
Sins are forgiven only after specific repentance
Only major sins are forgiven
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that when someone embraces Islam sincerely, Allah forgives all their past sins, showing the immense mercy of Allah towards new Muslims

questions.question: After embracing Islam, a person's good deeds are rewarded between ten to seven hundred times while evil deeds are recorded as one unless forgiven by Allah
options: False
True
questions.explanation: This accurately reflects the hadith's teaching about the multiplication of good deeds and the recording of evil deeds after sincere conversion to Islam

questions.question: How can this hadith inspire your daily practice as a Muslim?
options: Maintain sincerity in all actions and worship
Seek Allah's forgiveness regularly for any wrongdoings
All of the above
Strive to perform more good deeds knowing they are multiplied
questions.explanation: This hadith encourages us to appreciate Allah's mercy, increase good deeds, maintain sincerity, and regularly seek forgiveness - all essential aspects of strengthening our faith

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "If any one of you improve (follows strictly) his Islamic religion then his good deeds will be rewarded ten times to seven hundred times for each good deed and a bad deed will be recorded as it is."

questions.question: What is the main message about reward and punishment in this hadith?
options: Good deeds are multiplied while bad deeds are recorded as single
Only good deeds are recorded
All deeds are recorded equally
Bad deeds are multiplied like good deeds
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that good deeds are rewarded 10 to 700 times while bad deeds are recorded as single units

questions.question: According to this hadith, if someone strictly follows Islamic teachings, their minor sins will be automatically erased
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith states that bad deeds are still recorded as they are, but good deeds are multiplied for those who improve their Islamic practice

questions.question: How can you apply the wisdom of this hadith in your daily life?
options: Focus on increasing good deeds knowing they'll be multiplied
All of the above
Be careful about bad deeds since they're recorded exactly
Strive to improve my Islamic practice consistently
questions.explanation: This hadith encourages us to maximize good deeds, avoid bad deeds, and continuously improve our Islamic practice - all three applications are important

hadithText: Once the Prophet (ﷺ) came while a woman was sitting with me. He said, "Who is she?" I replied, "She is so and so," and told him about her (excessive) praying. He said disapprovingly, "Do (good) deeds which is within your capacity (without being overtaxed) as Allah does not get tired (of giving rewards) but (surely) you will get tired and the best deed (act of Worship) in the sight of Allah is that which is done regularly."
theme: Ad-Din (good, righteous deed - act of worship) loved most by Allah Jalla Jalalahu is that which is done regularly. (And in fact the best religion with Allah is Islam)

questions.question: What is the main message of this hadith regarding worship?
options: Only lengthy prayers are accepted by Allah
Consistent moderate deeds are better than excessive worship that leads to burnout
Women should avoid excessive praying
Allah prefers worship done in large gatherings
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) emphasized that regular, sustainable worship within one's capacity is superior to excessive acts that cause fatigue and abandonment

questions.question: According to this hadith, it is better to pray only occasionally but with great intensity rather than praying regularly within one's capacity
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that the best deed is that which is done regularly and consistently, not occasional intense worship

questions.question: How can you apply the wisdom from this hadith in your daily worship?
options: Balance worship with other responsibilities without burnout
Choose additional voluntary acts I can maintain regularly
All of the above
Establish consistent daily prayers rather than occasional long ones
questions.explanation: Applying this hadith means creating a sustainable worship routine that brings you closer to Allah without causing exhaustion or neglect of other duties

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Whoever said "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah and has in his heart good (faith) equal to the weight of a barley grain will be taken out of Hell. And whoever said: "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah and has in his heart good (faith) equal to the weight of a wheat grain will be taken out of Hell. And whoever said, "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah and has in his heart good (faith) equal to the weight of an atom will be taken out of Hell."

questions.question: What is the main message of this hadith regarding faith and salvation?
options: Only perfect faith guarantees salvation
Even the smallest amount of sincere faith can save from Hell
Faith alone without deeds is sufficient for salvation
Faith must be equal to wheat grain weight to be accepted
questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes that even an atom's weight of sincere faith in 'La ilaha illallah' can save a person from Hell, showing Allah's immense mercy

questions.question: According to this hadith, a person with even the smallest amount of genuine faith in their heart will eventually be taken out of Hell if they enter it
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Prophet explicitly stated that whoever has faith equal to an atom's weight will be taken out of Hell, demonstrating Allah's mercy for even minimal sincere faith

questions.question: How can you strengthen your faith after reflecting on this hadith?
options: Make dua for increased and firm faith
Regularly renew my shahadah with understanding
Study tawheed to deepen my belief
All of the above
questions.explanation: This hadith inspires us to continuously nurture and strengthen our faith through multiple means, as faith can increase and decrease

hadithText: Once a Jew said to me, "O the chief of believers! There is a verse in your Holy Book Which is read by all of you (Muslims), and had it been revealed to us, we would have taken that day (on which it was revealed as a day of celebration." 'Umar bin Al-Khattab asked, "Which is that verse?" The Jew replied, "This day I have perfected your religion For you, completed My favor upon you, And have chosen for you Islam as your religion." (5:3) 'Umar replied,"No doubt, we know when and where this verse was revealed to the Prophet. It was Friday and the Prophet (ﷺ) was standing at 'Arafat (i.e. the Day of Hajj)"

questions.question: What is the main significance of the verse mentioned in this hadith (Quran 5:3)?
options: It describes the relationship with Jews
It marks the completion of Islam as a perfect religion
It explains the rituals of Hajj
It discusses the importance of Friday prayers
questions.explanation: The verse declares the perfection and completion of Islam as a religion, which is why the Jew recognized its significance and said they would have celebrated its revelation

questions.question: According to this hadith, Muslims should celebrate the day this verse was revealed as an annual festival
options: True
False
questions.explanation: While the Jew suggested they would have celebrated it annually, Umar's response shows Muslims recognize its importance but don't establish new celebrations beyond what Islam has prescribed

questions.question: How can you demonstrate gratitude for the completion of Islam mentioned in this hadith?
options: By studying and understanding Islamic teachings deeply
By practicing Islam consistently in daily life
All of the above
By appreciating the completeness of Allah's guidance
questions.explanation: The perfection of Islam calls for comprehensive commitment - through knowledge, practice, and heartfelt appreciation of this divine favor

hadithText: A man from Najd with unkempt hair came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and we heard his loud voice but could not understand what he was saying, till he came near and then we came to know that he was asking about Islam. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "You have to offer prayers perfectly five times in a day and night (24 hours)." The man asked, "Is there any more (praying)?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "No, but if you want to offer the Nawafil prayers (you can)." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) further said to him: "You have to observe fasts during the month of Ramadan." The man asked, "Is there any more fasting?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "No, but if you want to observe the Nawafil fasts (you can.)" Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) further said to him, "You have to pay the Zakat (obligatory charity)." The man asked, "Is there any thing other than the Zakat for me to pay?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "No, unless you want to give alms of your own." And then that man retreated saying, "By Allah! I will neither do less nor more than this." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "If what he said is true, then he will be successful (i.e. he will be granted Paradise)."
theme: To pay Zakat is a part of Islam

questions.question: What is the main message about Islamic obligations conveyed in this hadith?
options: The five pillars of Islam are sufficient for salvation when fulfilled properly
Zakat is the most important pillar of Islam
Extra voluntary acts are required for salvation
Only prayer and fasting are essential for Muslims
questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes that fulfilling the obligatory acts (prayer, fasting, zakat) properly leads to success in the Hereafter, while voluntary acts are optional but beneficial

questions.question: According to this hadith, performing voluntary prayers and fasts is mandatory for all Muslims
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) clearly stated that nawafil (voluntary) prayers and fasts are optional, not obligatory, after the man asked if there were additional requirements beyond the fard (obligatory) acts

questions.question: How can you apply the lesson from this hadith in your daily practice of Islam?
options: Ignore voluntary acts completely
Focus on perfecting obligatory worship while considering voluntary acts as bonus
Prioritize voluntary acts over obligatory ones
Only perform the minimum required obligations
questions.explanation: The ideal approach is to ensure we fulfill our obligatory duties with excellence first, then add voluntary acts as we're able, following the balanced guidance of the Prophet (ﷺ)

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "(A believer) who accompanies the funeral procession of a Muslim out of sincere faith and hoping to attain Allah's reward and remains with it till the funeral prayer is offered and the burial ceremonies are over, he will return with a reward of two Qirats. Each Qirat is like the size of the (Mount) Uhud. He who offers the funeral prayer only and returns before the burial, will return with the reward of one Qirat only."
theme: To accompany the funeral processions (up to the place of burial) is a part of faith

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the main difference in reward between accompanying a funeral until burial versus only attending the prayer?
options: Double the reward for full accompaniment
No reward for partial attendance
Triple the reward for prayer only
Same reward for both actions
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that full accompaniment until burial completion earns two Qirats (each like Mount Uhud), while attending only the prayer earns one Qirat

questions.question: If you attend a Muslim's funeral prayer but leave before the burial, you still receive a significant reward according to this hadith
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) specified that even attending only the funeral prayer earns one Qirat, which is immense like Mount Uhud

questions.question: How can you implement the teachings of this hadith in your community?
options: Remind others of this great reward
Stay until burial when possible
All of the above
Make effort to attend Muslim funerals
questions.explanation: Full implementation involves consistent attendance, completion of burial rites when possible, and sharing this beneficial knowledge with others

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Abusing a Muslim is Fusuq (an evil doing) and killing him is Kufr (disbelief)."
theme: (What is said regarding) the fear of a believer that his good deeds may be annulled (lost) without his knowledge

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the spiritual status of killing a Muslim?
options: It constitutes disbelief (Kufr)
It is permissible in self-defense
It is a minor sin
It requires only repentance
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly stated that killing a Muslim is Kufr (disbelief), indicating the grave spiritual consequences of this action

questions.question: Verbally insulting another Muslim is considered Fusuq (evil doing) according to this hadith
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that abusing a Muslim is Fusuq, showing that even verbal harm has serious spiritual implications

questions.question: How will you apply the teachings of this hadith in your daily interactions?
options: I will guard my tongue from insulting others
All of the above
I will respect the sanctity of every Muslim's life
I will reflect on how my actions affect my spiritual state
questions.explanation: Applying this hadith requires comprehensive commitment to protecting both our speech and actions, while maintaining constant awareness of our spiritual standing

hadithText: "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went out to inform the people about the (date of the) night of decree (Al-Qadr) but there happened a quarrel between two Muslim men. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I came out to inform you about (the date of) the night of Al-Qadr, but as so and so and so and so quarrelled, its knowledge was taken away (I forgot it) and maybe it was better for you. Now look for it in the 7th, the 9th and the 5th (of the last 10 nights of the month of Ramadan)."

questions.question: According to this hadith, what caused the Prophet (ﷺ) to forget the exact date of Laylat al-Qadr?
options: Interruption by non-Muslims
A quarrel between two Muslims
Divine wisdom for people's benefit
His own forgetfulness
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that the knowledge was taken away when two Muslim men quarreled, showing how disputes among believers can affect spiritual blessings

questions.question: Based on this hadith, we should avoid arguments and conflicts during Ramadan to preserve spiritual blessings
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith demonstrates how quarrels can cause loss of divine knowledge and blessings, emphasizing the importance of maintaining peace and unity

questions.question: How will you apply the lessons from this hadith in your Ramadan practice?
options: I will reflect on how my actions affect spiritual opportunities
I will actively avoid arguments and seek reconciliation
All of the above
I will search for Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights as guided
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us multiple important lessons about maintaining unity, following prophetic guidance, and being mindful of how our behavior impacts spiritual rewards

hadithText: One day while the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting in the company of some people, (The angel) Gabriel came and asked, "What is faith?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, 'Faith is to believe in Allah, His angels, (the) meeting with Him, His Apostles, and to believe in Resurrection." Then he further asked, "What is Islam?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "To worship Allah Alone and none else, to offer prayers perfectly to pay the compulsory charity (Zakat) and to observe fasts during the month of Ramadan." Then he further asked, "What is Ihsan (perfection)?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "To worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you cannot achieve this state of devotion then you must consider that He is looking at you." Then he further asked, "When will the Hour be established?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "The answerer has no better knowledge than the questioner. But I will inform you about its portents. 1. When a slave (lady) gives birth to her master. 2. When the shepherds of black camels start boasting and competing with others in the construction of higher buildings. And the Hour is one of five things which nobody knows except Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) then recited: "Verily, with Allah (Alone) is the knowledge of the Hour--." (31. 34) Then that man (Gabriel) left and the Prophet (ﷺ) asked his companions to call him back, but they could not see him. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "That was Gabriel who came to teach the people their religion." Abu 'Abdullah said: He (the Prophet) considered all that as a part of faith.
theme: The asking of (angel) Jibrll (Gabriel) from the Prophet (saws) about Iman, Islam, Ihsan and the knowledge of the Hour

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the primary difference between Islam and Iman?
options: Islam focuses on angels while Iman focuses on prayer
Islam is for beginners while Iman is for advanced believers
Islam is about the Hour while Iman is about daily life
Islam refers to outward acts of worship while Iman refers to internal beliefs
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly distinguishes Islam as the five pillars (outward acts) and Iman as the six articles of faith (internal beliefs), showing they complement each other in forming complete faith

questions.question: Based on the hadith, a Muslim should pray their daily prayers with the consciousness that Allah is watching them, even if they cannot visualize Him
options: False
True
questions.explanation: This reflects the concept of Ihsan mentioned in the hadith - worshipping Allah as if you see Him, or at minimum being aware that He sees you

questions.question: How can you implement the teachings about Ihsan from this hadith in your daily worship?
options: By striving to perfect my worship as if standing before Allah
By remembering Allah's constant presence in all actions
By developing greater presence and mindfulness during prayers
All of the above
questions.explanation: Ihsan encompasses all these aspects - mindfulness, constant God-consciousness, and striving for excellence in worship as described by the Prophet

hadithText: I was informed by Abu Sufyan that Heraclius said to him, "I asked you whether they (followers of Muhammad) were increasing or decreasing. You replied that they were increasing. And in fact, this is the way of true Faith till it is complete in all respects. I further asked you whether there was anybody, who, after embracing his (the Prophets) religion (Islam) became displeased and discarded it. You replied in the negative, and in fact, this is (a sign of) true faith. When its delight enters the heart and mixes with them completely, nobody can be displeased with it."

questions.question: According to Heraclius' observations in this hadith, what are the two signs of true faith mentioned?
options: Political influence and military strength
Wealth and power of the community
Miracles and divine protection
Continuous increase in followers and no one leaving after embracing it
questions.explanation: Heraclius specifically mentions that true faith keeps increasing in followers and that once people embrace it sincerely, they never leave it because faith's delight mixes completely with their hearts

questions.question: A person who truly experiences the delight of faith in their heart would easily abandon Islam when facing difficulties
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that when faith's delight enters and mixes completely with the heart, nobody becomes displeased with it or discards it

questions.question: Based on this hadith's teaching about faith becoming complete when it mixes with the heart, how can you strengthen your own faith?
options: Seek to understand Islam deeply to experience its delight
Wait for faith to grow automatically without effort
Compare Islam with other religions frequently
Focus only on outward rituals without inner connection
questions.explanation: The correct approach is to actively seek deeper understanding and connection with Islamic teachings, as true faith becomes complete when it genuinely mixes with the heart and brings delight

hadithText: I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, 'Both legal and illegal things are evident but in between them there are doubtful (suspicious) things and most of the people have no knowledge about them. So whoever saves himself from these suspicious things saves his religion and his honor. And whoever indulges in these suspicious things is like a shepherd who grazes (his animals) near the Hima (private pasture) of someone else and at any moment he is liable to get in it. (O people!) Beware! Every king has a Hima and the Hima of Allah on the earth is His illegal (forbidden) things. Beware! There is a piece of flesh in the body if it becomes good (reformed) the whole body becomes good but if it gets spoilt the whole body gets spoilt and that is the heart.
theme: The superiority of that person who leaves all doubtful (unclear) things for the sake of his religion

questions.question: According to the hadith, what is the main reason for avoiding doubtful matters?
options: To appear more pious to others
To simplify daily decision-making
To avoid legal consequences
To protect one's religion and honor
questions.explanation: The Prophet explicitly states that whoever saves himself from suspicious things saves his religion and his honor

questions.question: Engaging in doubtful matters is compared to a shepherd grazing near someone else's private pasture, indicating the high risk of crossing into forbidden territory
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith uses this powerful analogy to show how easily one can slip from doubtful matters into clearly forbidden ones

questions.question: How will you apply the teachings of this hadith in your daily life?
options: All of the above
I will focus on purifying my heart as the key to overall righteousness
I will develop greater awareness of my intentions and actions
I will research and clarify any doubtful matters before acting
questions.explanation: This comprehensive approach addresses all key aspects of the hadith: avoiding doubtful matters, the heart's central role, and practical application

hadithText:
I used to sit with Ibn 'Abbas and he made me sit on his sitting place. He requested me to stay with him in order that he might give me a share from his property. So I stayed with him for two months. Once he told (me) that when the delegation of the tribe of 'Abdul Qais came to the Prophet, the Prophet (ﷺ) asked them, "Who are the people (i.e. you)? (Or) who are the delegate?" They replied, "We are from the tribe of Rabi'a." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them, "Welcome! O people (or O delegation of 'Abdul Qais)! Neither will you have disgrace nor will you regret." They said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! We cannot come to you except in the sacred month and there is the infidel tribe of Mudar intervening between you and us. So please order us to do something good (religious deeds) so that we may inform our people whom we have left behind (at home), and that we may enter Paradise (by acting on them)." Then they asked about drinks (what is legal and what is illegal). The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them to do four things and forbade them from four things. He ordered them to believe in Allah Alone and asked them, "Do you know what is meant by believing in Allah Alone?" They replied, "Allah and His Apostle know better." Thereupon the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "It means: 
1. To testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and Muhammad is Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). 
2. To offer prayers perfectly 
3. To pay the Zakat (obligatory charity) 
4. To observe fast during the month of Ramadan. 
5. And to pay Al-Khumus (one fifth of the booty to be given in Allah's Cause). 
Then he forbade them four things, namely, Hantam, Dubba,' Naqir Ann Muzaffat or Muqaiyar; (These were the names of pots in which Alcoholic drinks were prepared) (The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned the container of wine and he meant the wine itself). The Prophet (ﷺ) further said (to them): "Memorize them (these instructions) and convey them to the people whom you have left behind."
theme: To pay Al-Khumus (one-fifth of the war booty to be given in Allah's Cause) is a part of faith

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the delegation from 'Abdul Qais coming to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: To complain about political matters in their region
To seek military protection from enemy tribes
To learn essential Islamic teachings they could practice and teach others
To request financial assistance for their tribe
questions.explanation: The delegation specifically asked the Prophet to 'order us to do something good so that we may inform our people whom we have left behind' - showing their desire to learn and transmit Islamic teachings

questions.question: According to this hadith, paying Al-Khumus (one-fifth of war booty) is considered one of the pillars of Islam.
options: False
True
questions.explanation: While paying Al-Khumus is an important Islamic obligation mentioned in this hadith, it is not one of the five pillars of Islam. The pillars mentioned are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, and Hajj.

questions.question: How can you apply the lesson from this hadith in your daily life?
options: Share Islamic knowledge with others when possible
Be sincere in seeking religious knowledge despite obstacles
Memorize and practice the essential teachings of Islam
All of the above
questions.explanation: The delegation traveled through difficult circumstances to seek knowledge, then were instructed to memorize and convey it - inspiring us to value, practice, and share Islamic teachings in our lives

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "The reward of deeds depends upon the intention and every person will get the reward according to what he has intended. So whoever emigrated for Allah and His Apostle, then his emigration was for Allah and His Apostle. And whoever emigrated for worldly benefits or for a woman to marry, his emigration was for what he emigrated for."
theme: What is said regarding the statement: "The reward of deeds depends upon the intention and hoping to get rewards from Allah."

questions.question: According to this hadith, what primarily determines the reward of our deeds?
options: The visible outcome and results achieved
The sincerity and intention behind the action
The public recognition and praise received
The difficulty and effort put into the action
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly states that deeds are rewarded according to one's intention, emphasizing that the spiritual value of actions depends on their underlying purpose

questions.question: If two people perform the exact same good deed but with different intentions, they will receive the same reward from Allah.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that rewards differ based on intentions - someone who emigrates for Allah's pleasure gets a different reward than someone who emigrates for worldly gains, even if the physical action is identical

questions.question: How can you apply the lesson of this hadith in your daily worship?
options: Focus on seeking Allah's pleasure rather than people's praise
Regularly check and purify my intentions before any action
Remind myself that even small deeds with sincere intention are valuable
All of the above
questions.explanation: Applying this hadith requires comprehensive effort - constantly examining intentions, prioritizing Allah's pleasure over worldly recognition, and valuing sincerity in all deeds, big or small

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If a man spends on his family (with the intention of having a reward from Allah) sincerely for Allah's sake then it is a (kind of) alms-giving in reward for him.

questions.question: What is the main condition mentioned in this hadith for spending on one's family to be considered a rewardable act?
options: Spending large amounts of money
Sincere intention for Allah's sake
Only spending on essential items
Getting approval from family members
questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes that sincere intention for Allah's sake transforms ordinary family spending into a rewardable act of charity

questions.question: According to this hadith, buying groceries for your family with the intention of pleasing Allah counts as an act of charity
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that any spending on family with sincere intention for Allah's sake becomes a form of sadaqah (charity)

questions.question: How can you implement the teaching of this hadith in your daily life?
options: All of the above
Be grateful for the chance to earn rewards through family responsibilities
View family expenses as opportunities for spiritual reward
Renew my intention before providing for family needs
questions.explanation: Implementing all these approaches will help transform your family responsibilities into continuous acts of worship and charity

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "You will be rewarded for whatever you spend for Allah's sake even if it were a morsel which you put in your wife's mouth."

questions.question: What is the main message of this hadith about spending for Allah's sake?
options: Feeding your wife is the only act that brings reward
Only large charitable donations to mosques are rewarded by Allah
Even small acts of kindness to family members are rewarded when done with sincere intention
Rewards are only given for spending on strangers, not family
questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes that any spending done for Allah's sake, no matter how small and even within one's own family, brings divine reward when intention is pure

questions.question: According to this hadith, feeding your spouse with a small piece of food can earn you reward from Allah if done with the right intention
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically mentions that even a morsel of food given to one's wife with the intention of pleasing Allah brings reward

questions.question: How can you apply the teaching of this hadith in your daily family life?
options: I will purify my intention when providing for my family members
I will recognize all small acts of kindness to family as opportunities for reward
All of the above
I will appreciate that serving my family is a form of worship
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us to transform ordinary family care into continuous worship by maintaining sincere intention for Allah's pleasure in all our actions

hadithText:
I gave the pledge of allegiance to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) for the following: 
1. offer prayers perfectly 
2. pay the Zakat (obligatory charity) 
3. and be sincere and true to every Muslim.
theme: The statement of the Prophet (saws): Religion is An-Nasihah (to be sincere and true) to Allah, to His Messenger (Muhammad (saws)), to the Muslim rulers, and to all the Muslims

questions.question: What is the main message of this hadith regarding the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: It emphasizes political loyalty above all else
It focuses only on individual prayer and charity
It combines worship of Allah with sincere treatment of fellow Muslims
It is primarily about financial obligations to the community
questions.explanation: The hadith beautifully connects our duties to Allah (prayer and zakat) with our responsibilities toward fellow Muslims (sincerity and truthfulness), showing that true faith encompasses both vertical and horizontal relationships

questions.question: According to this hadith, being sincere and true to fellow Muslims means we should avoid backbiting, honor our promises, and wish for them what we wish for ourselves
options: True
False
questions.explanation: This statement reflects the practical application of being 'sincere and true to every Muslim' which includes avoiding harm, keeping commitments, and having genuine goodwill

questions.question: How will you personally apply the teachings of this hadith in your daily life?
options: I will perfect my prayers and pay zakat when due
I will be more conscious of my treatment and sincerity toward other Muslims
All of the above
I will study what true sincerity (nasihah) means in Islamic teachings
questions.explanation: Excellent! A comprehensive approach to implementing this hadith involves improving worship, enhancing interpersonal relationships, and deepening your understanding of Islamic concepts

hadithText: I heard Jarir bin 'Abdullah (Praising Allah). On the day when Al-Mughira bin Shu'ba died, he (Jarir) got up (on the pulpit) and thanked and praised Allah and said, "Be afraid of Allah alone Who has none along with Him to be worshipped.(You should) be calm and quiet till the (new) chief comes to you and he will come to you soon. Ask Allah's forgiveness for your (late) chief because he himself loved to forgive others." Jarir added, "Amma badu (now then), I went to the Prophet and said, 'I give my pledge of allegiance to you for Islam." The Prophet (ﷺ) conditioned (my pledge) for me to be sincere and true to every Muslim so I gave my pledge to him for this. By the Lord of this mosque! I am sincere and true to you (Muslims). Then Jarir asked for Allah's forgiveness and came down (from the pulpit).

questions.question: What is the primary lesson about character from Jarir bin Abdullah's speech after Al-Mughira's death?
options: Only prophets can demand pledges of allegiance
Muslims should maintain sincerity and loyalty to fellow believers
People should mourn loudly when leaders die
Leaders should always give speeches from the pulpit
questions.explanation: Jarir emphasized his pledge to the Prophet to be sincere and true to every Muslim, highlighting the importance of genuine brotherhood and loyalty in Islamic character

questions.question: According to this hadith, when a Muslim leader passes away, we should immediately panic and demand a new leader
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Jarir advised people to 'be calm and quiet till the new chief comes' and to ask Allah's forgiveness for the deceased leader, showing the importance of patience and proper conduct during leadership transitions

questions.question: How can you implement the character lessons from this hadith in your daily life?
options: Be sincere in my dealings with all Muslims
Practice patience during community transitions
Seek forgiveness for others as I would for myself
All of the above
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches multiple aspects of noble character - sincerity to fellow Muslims, patience in difficult times, and seeking forgiveness for others - all of which we should strive to implement

hadithText: While the Prophet (ﷺ) was saying something in a gathering, a Bedouin came and asked him, "When would the Hour (Doomsday) take place?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) continued his talk, so some people said that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had heard the question, but did not like what that Bedouin had asked. Some of them said that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had not heard it. When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished his speech, he said, "Where is the questioner, who inquired about the Hour (Doomsday)?" The Bedouin said, "I am here, O Allah's Apostle ." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "When honesty is lost, then wait for the Hour (Doomsday)." The Bedouin said, "How will that be lost?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "When the power or authority comes in the hands of unfit persons, then wait for the Hour (Doomsday.)"
theme: Whoever is asked about knowledge while he is busy in some conversation, so he finished talking and then answered the questioner

questions.question: According to this hadith, what is the primary sign that indicates the approaching of the Hour (Doomsday)?
options: When wealth becomes concentrated among few people
When people stop praying regularly
When honesty is lost and authority is given to unfit persons
When natural disasters increase worldwide
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) clearly stated that the loss of honesty and authority falling into unfit hands are key signs of the approaching Hour

questions.question: If someone interrupts your important conversation with a question, you should immediately stop and answer them without finishing your thoughts.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) demonstrated the proper etiquette by finishing his speech before addressing the Bedouin's question, showing we should complete our current conversation respectfully

questions.question: Based on this hadith's teachings, how can you personally contribute to delaying the signs of the Hour in your community?
options: By practicing honesty in all my dealings and supporting qualified leadership
By avoiding positions of responsibility to prevent unfit leadership
By frequently discussing the signs of Doomsday with others
By focusing only on my personal worship and ignoring community affairs
questions.explanation: The most comprehensive application is to embody honesty and support qualified leadership, directly countering the signs mentioned in the hadith

hadithText: Once the Prophet (ﷺ) remained behind us in a journey. He joined us while we were performing ablution for the prayer which was over-due. We were just passing wet hands over our feet (and not washing them properly) so the Prophet (ﷺ) addressed us in a loud voice and said twice or thrice: "Save your heels from the fire."
theme: Whoever raises his voice in (conveying) knowledge

questions.question: What is the primary lesson from the Prophet's warning about the heels in this hadith?
options: Keep feet clean for hygiene purposes
Complete all required actions in worship without negligence
Avoid walking barefoot on hot surfaces
Wear proper footwear during travel
questions.explanation: The Prophet emphasized performing ablution completely, warning against neglecting any part of it, as incomplete worship can have spiritual consequences

questions.question: When performing wudu (ablution), it is sufficient to just pass wet hands over the feet without properly washing them.
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith clearly shows that proper washing of feet is required in ablution, as the Prophet corrected the companions who were only passing wet hands over their feet

questions.question: How will you ensure you properly implement the lesson from this hadith in your daily prayers?
options: I will carefully wash all required body parts completely during wudu
I will remind myself that incomplete worship may deprive me of full rewards
I will learn the proper method of ablution from authentic sources
All of the above
questions.explanation: Implementing all these actions demonstrates comprehensive understanding and commitment to performing worship properly as taught by the Prophet

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Amongst the trees, there is a tree, the leaves of which do not fall and is like a Muslim. Tell me the name of that tree." Everybody started thinking about the trees of the desert areas. And I thought of the date-palm tree but felt shy to answer the others then asked, "What is that tree, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ?" He replied, "It is the date-palm tree."
theme: Concerning the variety of words used by narrators conveying different significations regarding the concept of narrating and which has importance for the Hadith scholars only

questions.question: According to the hadith, what quality of the date-palm tree makes it comparable to a Muslim?
options: It produces sweet fruit, symbolizing good deeds
It grows in the desert, representing resilience
Its leaves do not fall, symbolizing steadfast faith
It grows tall, representing spiritual elevation
questions.explanation: The Prophet specifically mentioned that the tree's leaves do not fall, representing how a Muslim's faith remains constant and doesn't wither away

questions.question: A Muslim should strive to maintain consistent faith and good character throughout all seasons of life, just like the date-palm tree maintains its leaves year-round
options: False
True
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches us that Muslims should be steadfast in faith and character, not changing with circumstances like trees that shed leaves seasonally

questions.question: How can you embody the lesson of this hadith in your daily life?
options: All of the above
Continue learning and growing in faith continuously
Stay firm in Islamic principles when facing challenges
Maintain consistent worship regardless of circumstances
questions.explanation: The date-palm tree represents comprehensive steadfastness - we should apply this to all aspects of our faith journey

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Amongst the trees, there is a tree, the leaves of which do not fall and is like a Muslim. Tell me the name of that tree." Everybody started thinking about the trees of the desert areas. And I thought of the date-palm tree. The others then asked, "Please inform us what is that tree, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" He replied, "It is the date-palm tree."
theme: The Imam questioning his companions in order to test their knowledge

questions.question: What quality of the date-palm tree makes it comparable to a true Muslim according to this hadith?
options: It grows in the desert, representing resilience
It provides dates, symbolizing good deeds
Its leaves never fall, symbolizing steadfast faith
It grows tall, representing spiritual elevation
questions.explanation: The Prophet specifically mentioned that the tree's leaves do not fall, representing how a Muslim's faith remains constant and unwavering through all seasons of life

questions.question: A Muslim should maintain consistent faith and good character regardless of changing circumstances, just like the date-palm tree maintains its leaves throughout the year
options: False
True
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us that true Muslims remain steadfast in their faith and practice, not allowing external conditions to weaken their commitment to Islam

questions.question: How can you embody the lesson of this hadith in your daily life?
options: Keep learning about Islam despite busy schedule
Continue giving charity when facing financial challenges
All of the above
Maintain regular prayers even during difficult times
questions.explanation: Being like the date-palm tree means demonstrating unwavering commitment to Islamic practices in all circumstances - this comprehensive approach reflects true steadfastness

hadithText: While we were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) in the mosque, a man came riding on a camel. He made his camel kneel down in the mosque, tied its foreleg and then said: "Who amongst you is Muhammad?" At that time the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting amongst us (his companions) leaning on his arm. We replied, "This white man reclining on his arm." The man then addressed him, "O Son of `Abdul Muttalib." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I am here to answer your questions." The man said to the Prophet, "I want to ask you something and will be hard in questioning. So do not get angry." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Ask whatever you want." The man said, "I ask you by your Lord, and the Lord of those who were before you, has Allah sent you as an Apostle to all the mankind?" The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "By Allah, yes." The man further said, "I ask you by Allah. Has Allah ordered you to offer five prayers in a day and night (24 hours).? He replied, "By Allah, Yes." The man further said, "I ask you by Allah! Has Allah ordered you to observe fasts during this month of the year (i.e. Ramadan)?" He replied, "By Allah, Yes." The man further said, "I ask you by Allah. Has Allah ordered you to take Zakat (obligatory charity) from our rich people and distribute it amongst our poor people?" The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "By Allah, yes." Thereupon that man said, "I have believed in all that with which you have been sent, and I have been sent by my people as a messenger, and I am Dimam bin Tha`laba from the brothers of Bani Sa`d bin Bakr."

questions.question: What was the main purpose of Dimam bin Tha'laba's questioning of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?
options: To request financial assistance for his tribe
To learn about the Prophet's family background
To verify the fundamental pillars of Islam before accepting them
To challenge the Prophet's authority and prove him wrong
questions.explanation: Dimam bin Tha'laba asked specific questions about the core Islamic pillars - belief in prophethood, prayer, fasting, and zakat - to confirm their divine origin before embracing Islam himself and representing his people

questions.question: When someone approaches us with sincere questions about Islam, even if they seem direct or challenging, we should respond with patience and clarity just as the Prophet (ﷺ) did with Dimam.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Prophet (ﷺ) demonstrated perfect patience when Dimam warned he would be 'hard in questioning,' showing us how to handle sincere inquiries about our faith with grace and wisdom

questions.question: How can you apply the lesson from this hadith in your own journey of Islamic learning?
options: I will share verified Islamic teachings with others after confirming them
All of the above
I will seek authentic knowledge about Islam's fundamental pillars
I will approach knowledgeable people with respect when seeking clarification
questions.explanation: This hadith teaches us the importance of seeking knowledge properly, verifying religious matters, and sharing authentic teachings - all essential for strengthening our faith and helping others

hadithText: Once Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) gave a letter to a person and ordered him to go and deliver it to the Governor of Bahrain. (He did so) and the Governor of Bahrain sent it to Chousroes, who read that letter and then tore it to pieces. (The sub-narrator (Ibn Shihab) thinks that Ibn Al-Musaiyab said that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) invoked Allah against them (saying), "May Allah tear them into pieces, and disperse them all totally.)"
theme: What is said regarding the hand to hand exchange (of books of knowledge), and the writing of knowledge by religious scholars to different countries

questions.question: What is the primary lesson about conveying Islamic knowledge demonstrated in this hadith?
options: Muslims should courageously deliver Islamic teachings even to hostile rulers
Knowledge should be kept secret from non-Muslims
Letters should only be sent to friendly governments
Messengers should avoid dangerous missions
questions.explanation: The hadith shows Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) actively sending Islamic teachings to the ruler of Bahrain despite potential rejection, demonstrating the importance of conveying knowledge even when facing opposition

questions.question: Based on this hadith, Muslims should only share Islamic knowledge with those who are likely to accept it
options: True
False
questions.explanation: False - The Prophet sent the letter knowing it might be rejected, showing our duty is to convey the message regardless of the recipient's response

questions.question: How can you apply the lesson of this hadith in your daily life?
options: Study Islamic teachings more deeply to share them accurately
All of the above
Share Islamic knowledge respectfully even when facing potential rejection
Support efforts to spread authentic Islamic knowledge globally
questions.explanation: All these actions reflect the hadith's spirit of courageously and actively sharing Islamic knowledge with others, following the Prophet's example

hadithText: Once the Prophet (ﷺ) wrote a letter or had an idea of writing a letter. The Prophet (ﷺ) was told that they (rulers) would not read letters unless they were sealed. So the Prophet (ﷺ) got a silver ring made with "Muhammad Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)" engraved on it. As if I were just observing its white glitter in the hand of the Prophet.

questions.question: What is the primary lesson from the Prophet's action of getting a seal ring engraved with 'Muhammad Allah's Messenger'?
options: Using expensive materials to impress rulers
Adapting methods while maintaining Islamic identity to effectively convey the message
Avoiding written communication entirely
Changing the message to suit different audiences
questions.explanation: The Prophet demonstrated wisdom by adapting to cultural expectations of sealed letters while firmly maintaining his Islamic identity and message

questions.question: When communicating Islamic teachings in professional or formal settings, we should consider adapting our presentation methods while keeping the core message unchanged
options: False
True
questions.explanation: This follows the Prophet's example of understanding his audience's expectations and adapting delivery methods without compromising Islamic principles

questions.question: How can you apply the lesson from this hadith in your daily interactions?
options: Study effective communication methods used by the Prophet
Adapt communication style to different audiences while maintaining Islamic values
Proudly display my Islamic identity in all situations
All of the above
questions.explanation: All these actions reflect the comprehensive wisdom of the Prophet's approach - balancing identity, adaptation, and continuous learning

hadithText: While Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was sitting in the mosque with some people, three men came. Two of them came in front of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and the third one went away. The two persons kept on standing before Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) for a while and then one of them found a place in the circle and sat there while the other sat behind the gathering, and the third one went away. When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) finished his preaching, he said, "Shall I tell you about these three persons? One of them betook himself to Allah, so Allah took him into His grace and mercy and accommodated him, the second felt shy from Allah, so Allah sheltered Him in His mercy (and did not punish him), while the third turned his face from Allah and went away, so Allah turned His face from him likewise. "
theme: Whoever sat at the farther end of a gathering. And whoever found a place amongst a gathering and took his seat there

questions.question: What is the main lesson from this hadith about joining gatherings?
options: How we join gatherings reflects our relationship with Allah
We should always sit in the front row
Only scholars should sit near the Prophet
Large gatherings are discouraged in Islam
questions.explanation: The hadith shows that our approach to joining gatherings - whether we actively seek knowledge, feel shy but still participate, or completely turn away - reflects our spiritual state and relationship with Allah

questions.question: If you arrive late to a religious gathering and find limited space, it's better to sit wherever you can find a spot rather than leave completely
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that even sitting at the back is better than leaving completely, as shown by the second man who felt shy but still joined the gathering and received Allah's mercy

questions.question: Based on this hadith, how will you improve your approach to religious gatherings?
options: Reflect on my intention when attending gatherings
All of the above
Always join even if I have to sit at the back
Arrive early to secure a good spot
questions.explanation: Implementing all these practices will help you follow the sunnah demonstrated in this hadith and strengthen your connection with Allah through seeking knowledge

hadithText: Once the Prophet (ﷺ) was riding his camel and a man was holding its rein. The Prophet (ﷺ) asked, "What is the day today?" We kept quiet, thinking that he might give that day another name. He said, "Isn't it the day of Nahr (slaughtering of the animals of sacrifice)" We replied, "Yes." He further asked, "Which month is this?" We again kept quiet, thinking that he might give it another name. Then he said, "Isn't it the month of Dhul-Hijja?" We replied, "Yes." He said, "Verily! Your blood, property and honor are sacred to one another (i.e. Muslims) like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours and in this city of yours. It is incumbent upon those who are present to inform those who are absent because those who are absent might comprehend (what I have said) better than the present audience."
theme: The Statement of the Prophet (saws): lt is probable that a person who receives a piece of information indirectly may comprehend it better than he who has heard it directly from its source

questions.question: What is the primary message the Prophet (ﷺ) emphasized in this hadith?
options: The sanctity of Muslim lives, property, and honor is as sacred as the Day of Nahr, month of Dhul-Hijja, and city of Makkah
The importance of correctly identifying Islamic dates and months
The superiority of those who receive knowledge indirectly over those who hear it directly
The proper method of animal sacrifice during Hajj
questions.explanation: The Prophet explicitly compared the sanctity of Muslim lives, property, and honor to the sacredness of the Day of Nahr, month of Dhul-Hijja, and Makkah, making this the core message

questions.question: According to this hadith, if you hear someone spreading false rumors about another Muslim's character, you should remain silent to avoid conflict
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that a Muslim's honor is sacred, so spreading or tolerating false rumors violates this sacred trust

questions.question: How will you personally apply the teachings of this hadith in your daily life?
options: I will respect others' property and not take what doesn't belong to me
I will protect fellow Muslims' honor by not backbiting or spreading rumors
All of the above
I will share this important teaching with others who haven't heard it
questions.explanation: Applying this hadith requires protecting all three sacred aspects (life, property, honor) and fulfilling the Prophet's instruction to convey the message to others

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to take care of us in preaching by selecting a suitable time, so that we might not get bored. (He abstained from pestering us with sermons and knowledge all the time).
theme: The Prophet (saws) used to take care of the people in preaching by selecting a suitable time so that they might not run away (never made them averse or bored them with religious talk and knowledge all the time)

questions.question: What is the main lesson from this hadith about the Prophet's teaching method?
options: He carefully timed his teachings to avoid boring his listeners
He only taught during formal gatherings
He taught continuously throughout the day
He avoided teaching complex topics
questions.explanation: The hadith specifically mentions the Prophet selected suitable times for preaching to prevent boredom and aversion to religious knowledge

questions.question: When sharing Islamic knowledge with others, we should deliver long lectures regardless of the audience's attention span
options: False
True
questions.explanation: This contradicts the hadith's teaching that we should be considerate of listeners' capacity and avoid overwhelming them

questions.question: How can you apply the wisdom from this hadith in your daily interactions?
options: Choose appropriate moments to share Islamic reminders
Observe when others are most receptive to learning
Avoid overwhelming people with continuous religious talk
All of the above
questions.explanation: Following the Prophet's example means being mindful of timing, receptiveness, and moderation in all our teaching and reminder efforts

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Facilitate things to people (concerning religious matters), and do not make it hard for them and give them good tidings and do not make them run away (from Islam).

questions.question: What is the primary message of this hadith regarding religious guidance?
options: Be strict in enforcing religious rules
Avoid giving religious advice to beginners
Focus only on advanced religious knowledge
Make Islam easy and approachable for people

hadithText: `Abdullah used to give a religious talk to the people on every Thursday. Once a man said, "O Aba `Abdur-Rahman! (By Allah) I wish if you could preach us daily." hadithText: I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "If Allah wants to do good to a person, He makes him comprehend the religion. I am just a distributor, but the grant is from Allah. (And remember) that this nation (true Muslims) will keep on following Allah's teachings strictly and they will not be harmed by any one going on a different path till Allah's order (Day of Judgment) is established."

hadithText: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) and fresh dates of a palm tree were brought to him. On that he said, "Amongst the trees, there is a tree which resembles a Muslim." I wanted to say that it was the datepalm tree but as I was the youngest of all (of them) I kept quiet. And then the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "It is the date-palm tree."

We should remain silent and listen when elders or scholars are speaking

questions.question: When attending Islamic lectures, it's better to listen attentively first rather than immediately speaking out what we think we know

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Do not wish to be like anyone except in two cases. (The first is) A person, whom Allah has given wealth and he spends it righteously; (the second is) the one whom Allah has given wisdom (the Holy Qur'an) and he acts according to it and teaches it to others." (Fath-al-Bari page 177 Vol. 1)

questions.question: According to this hadith, in which two cases are we permitted to wish to be like someone else?

questions.question: It is permissible to wish to be like someone who has memorized the entire Quran but doesn't practice its teachings

hadithText: That he differed with Hur bin Qais bin Hisn Al-Fazari regarding the companion of (the Prophet) Moses. Ibn `Abbas said that he was Al Khadir. Meanwhile, Ubai bin Ka`b passed by them and Ibn `Abbas called him, saying "My friend (Hur) and I have differed regarding Moses' companion, whom Moses asked the way to meet. Have you heard the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioning something about him? He said, "Yes. I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "While Moses was sitting in the company of some Israelites, a man came and asked him. "Do you know anyone who is more learned than you? Moses replied: "No." So Allah sent the Divine Inspiration to Moses: 'Yes, Our slave Khadir (is more learned than you.)' Moses asked (Allah) how to meet him (Khadir). So Allah made the fish as a sign for him and he was told that when the fish was lost, he should return (to the place where he had lost it) and there he would meet him (Al-Khadir). So Moses went on looking for the sign of the fish in the sea. The servant-boy of Moses said to him: Do you remember when we betook ourselves to the rock, I indeed forgot the fish, none but Satan made me forget to remember it. On that Moses said: 'That is what we have been seeking? (18.64) So they went back retracing their footsteps, and found Khadir. (And) what happened further to them is narrated in the Holy Qur'an by Allah. (18.54 up to 18.82)
theme: What has been said about the journey of Prophet Musa ('alaihi as-salam) (when he went) in the sea to meet Al-Khidr

questions.question: What is the main lesson about knowledge from this hadith?
options: Religious knowledge is superior to worldly knowledge
Scholars should never admit when others know more
No one possesses complete knowledge except Allah
Knowledge is only valuable when it's practical

questions.question: When someone corrects our misunderstanding of Islamic knowledge, we should accept it humbly like Ibn Abbas did when Ubai bin Ka'b clarified about Khadir
options: True

hadithText: Once I came riding a she-ass and had (just) attained the age of puberty. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was offering the prayer at Mina. There was no wall in front of him and I passed in front of some of the row while they were offering their prayers. There I let the she-ass loose to graze and entered the row, and nobody objected to it.

hadithText: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The example of guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like abundant rain falling on the earth, some of which was fertile soil that absorbed rain water and brought forth vegetation and grass in abundance. (And) another portion of it was hard and held the rain water and Allah benefited the people with it and they utilized it for drinking, making their animals drink from it and for irrigation of the land for cultivation. (And) a portion of it was barren which could neither hold the water nor bring forth vegetation (then that land gave no benefits). The first is the example of the person who comprehends Allah's religion and gets benefit (from the knowledge) which Allah has revealed through me (the Prophets and learns and then teaches others. The last example is that of a person who does not care for it and does not take Allah's guidance revealed through me (He is like that barren land.)"
theme: The superiority of a person who learns (Islam, becomes a religious scholar) and then teaches it to others

questions.question: What is the main message of this hadith about different types of people receiving Islamic knowledge?

All people benefit equally from Islamic knowledge regardless of their background

hadithText:

hadithText:

hadithText: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) stopped (for a while near the Jimar) at Mina during his last Hajj for the people and they were asking him questions. A man came and said, "I forgot and got my head shaved before slaughtering the Hadi (sacrificing animal)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "There is no harm, go and do the slaughtering now." Then another person came and said, "I forgot and slaughtered (the camel) before Rami (throwing of the pebbles) at the Jamra." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Do the Rami now and there is no harm." The narrator added: So on that day, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about anything (as regards the ceremonies of Hajj) performed before or after its due time, his reply was: "Do it (now) and there is no harm."

hadithText: I came to `Aisha while she was praying, and said to her, "What has happened to the people?" She pointed out towards the sky. (I looked towards the mosque), and saw the people offering the prayer. Aisha said, "Subhan Allah." I said to her, "Is there a sign?" She nodded with her head meaning, "Yes." I, too, then stood (for the prayer of eclipse) till I became (nearly) unconscious and later on I poured water on my head. After the prayer, the Prophet (ﷺ) praised and glorified Allah and then said, "Just now at this place I have seen what I have never seen before, including Paradise and Hell. No doubt it has been inspired to me that you will be put to trials in your graves and these trials will be like the trials of Masih-ad-Dajjal or nearly like it (the sub narrator is not sure which expression Asma' used). You will be asked, 'What do you know about this man (the Prophet (ﷺ) Muhammad)?' Then the faithful believer (or Asma' said a similar word) will reply, 'He is Muhammad Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) who had come to us with clear evidences and guidance and so we accepted his teachings and followed him. And he is Muhammad.' And he will repeat it thrice. Then the angels will say to him, 'Sleep in peace as we have come to know that you were a faithful believer.' On the other hand, a hypocrite or a doubtful person will reply, 'I do not know, but I heard the people saying something and so I said it.' (the same). "

hadithText: I was an interpreter between the people and Ibn `Abbas. Once Ibn `Abbas said that a delegation of the tribe of `Abdul Qais came to the Prophet (ﷺ) who asked them, "Who are the people (i.e. you)? (Or) who are the delegates?" They replied, "We are from the tribe of Rabi`a." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them, "Welcome, O people (or said, "O delegation (of `Abdul Qais).") Neither will you have disgrace nor will you regret." They said, "We have come to you from a distant place and there is the tribe of the infidels of Mudar intervening between you and us and we cannot come to you except in the sacred month. So please order us to do something good (religious deeds) and that we may also inform our people whom we have left behind (at home) and that we may enter Paradise (by acting on them.)" The Prophet ordered them to do four things, and forbade them from four things. He ordered them to believe in Allah Alone, the Honorable the Majestic and said to them, "Do you know what is meant by believing in Allah Alone?" They replied, "Allah and His Apostle know better." Thereupon the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "(That means to testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and that Muhammad is His Apostle, to offer prayers perfectly, to pay Zakat, to observe fasts during the month of Ramadan, (and) to pay Al-Khumus (one fifth of the booty to be given in Allah's cause)." Then he forbade them four things, namely Ad-Dubba.' Hantam, Muzaffat (and) An-Naqir or Muqaiyar (These were the names of pots in which alcoholic drinks used to be prepared). The Prophet (ﷺ) further said, "Memorize them (these instructions) and tell them to the people whom you have left behind."
theme: The Prophet (saws) urged the people (mission) of 'Abdul Qais to memorize the faith and the (religious) knowledge (as he explained to them) and to inform (convey) to their people whom they left behind (at home)

Avoid intoxicants and their means of preparation

hadithText: `Uqba bin Al-Harith said that he had married the daughter of Abi Ihab bin `Aziz. Later on a woman came to him and said, "I have suckled (nursed) `Uqba and the woman whom he married (his wife) at my breast." `Uqba said to her, "Neither I knew that you have suckled (nursed) me nor did you tell me." Then he rode over to see Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) at Medina, and asked him about it. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "How can you keep her as a wife when it has been said (that she is your foster-sister)?" Then `Uqba divorced her, and she married another man.

questions.explanation: The hadith demonstrates that such a marriage becomes invalid and requires immediate action, as shown by Uqba's journey to Medina and subsequent divorce

hadithText: My Ansari neighbor from Bani Umaiya bin Zaid who used to live at `Awali Al-Medina and used to visit the Prophet (ﷺ) by turns. He used to go one day and I another day. When I went I used to bring the news of that day regarding the Divine Inspiration and other things, and when he went, he used to do the same for me. Once my Ansari friend, in his turn (on returning from the Prophet), knocked violently at my door and asked if I was there." I became horrified and came out to him. He said, "Today a great thing has happened." I then went to Hafsa and saw her weeping. I asked her, "Did Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) divorce you all?" She replied, "I do not know." Then, I entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and said while standing, "Have you divorced your wives?" The Prophet (ﷺ) replied in the negative. On that I said, "Allahu-Akbar (Allah is Greater)." hadithText: A man asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the picking up of a "Luqata" (fallen lost thing). Then the person asked about the lost camel. On that, the Prophet (ﷺ) got angry and his cheeks or his Face became red and he said, "You have no concern with it as it has its water container, and its feet and it will reach water, and eat (the leaves) of trees till its owner finds it." The man then asked about the lost sheep. The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "It is either for you, for your brother (another person) or for the wolf."
